Title: Trump rejects Iran peace proposal, plans renewed bombing after US elections: WSJ
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump has rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting within seven days, and told aides he expects to resume bombing after November congressional elections, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing unnamed US officials.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi had told reporters at the United Nations on Friday that Iran conveyed its peace plan to the US through Qatari mediators, saying a deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.
"If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araqchi said.
A US official had told Reuters that the US and and Iran were having "positive and constructive discussions through the mediators," but Trump was privately skeptical that Iran that would meet his demands, the Journal report said.
He has told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely, the Journal said.
Reuters could not immediately confirm the report.
Diplomatic efforts surrounding the UN General Assembly in New York underscored the global stakes of the seven-month-old conflict, which has disrupted oil flows through one of the world's most critical shipping lanes and drawn in regional and world powers.
If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects," Araqchi said. Tehran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon. The plan in turn requires the United States to lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran's frozen funds, and waive its oil sanctions.
RETURN TO DIPLOMACY?
The Iranian seven-day proposal comes after previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on Feb 28 with US and Israeli strikes.
Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.
Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests. Iranian-aligned militias in Iraq were blamed for a pipeline attack that temporarily took more Saudi oil off the market. All the while, Iranian-backed Hizbollah has been engaged with Israeli forces in Lebanon.
With the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised Yemeni government under assault from Iran-linked Houthi fighters, and Houthi missiles striking inside Saudi Arabia, allies of the kingdom have united to show support.
Defense officials of Turkiye and Pakistan, both partners in a joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia, met in Riyadh on Friday to review the security situation and discuss intelligence cooperation, military coordination, and integrating forces, the Saudi defence ministry said in a statement.
The statement came a day after Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish foreign ministers met within the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
The violence in Yemen has prompted a new humanitarian crisis, the United Nations children's agency said on Friday, reporting a rise in acute malnutrition among children.--REUTERS

Title: Malaysia calls for reform of international financial system, multilateral trade
Article:
NEW YORK: Malaysia has called for reforms to international financial institutions and a more effective multilateral trading system for developing countries.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said developing countries needed to play a meaningful role in shaping the future direction of these systems.
"Malaysia calls for reforms to international financial institutions, a more effective multilateral trading system, stronger climate action and closer cooperation in science, technology and innovation, including information and communications technology and next-generation artificial intelligence," he said.
He said this in his intervention speech at the Group of 77 and China Ministerial Meeting held in conjunction with the 81st United Nations General Assembly here today.
He also said that any reform of the UN system should strengthen its ability to meet the needs of member states, particularly developing countries.
He said Global South cooperation demonstrated that developing countries were not merely recipients of development solutions, but also strategic partners and contributors to global development.
"Malaysia's commitment to Global South cooperation is reflected through the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme, which supports capacity building, technical cooperation and the sharing of expertise among developing countries," he said.
Mohamad said emerging challenges such as climate change, development financing and rapid technological transformation needed to be addressed without creating new gaps to replace existing ones.

Title: US networks return to White House pool as Trump media battle rages on
Article:
WASHINGTON: US television networks resumed coverage of President Donald Trump's White House events on Friday, providing the first live pool access for Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit, as a legal battle continues over restrictions on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
Trump last week banned the three outlets from the White House, before a judge ordered the administration to restore their access.
The White House television press pool aired video of Xi's arrival at the White House for tea on the final day of the Chinese leader's visit, as well as the two leaders' tour of the National Archives, which houses the US Constitution.
CNN, ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC share the costs of covering the president and rotate coverage, providing pool footage to other outlets. The other networks' refusal to set up cameras in solidarity meant there was no pool coverage of the first two days of Xi's visit.
The Washington Post reported on Friday evening that the White House had blocked CNN from traveling with Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee, citing unnamed sources. Neither the White House nor a spokesperson at CNN immediately responded to requests for comment from Reuters.
Trump has long relied on the media to shape his public image and advance his agenda, even as he regularly casts news organizations as political adversaries. Since returning to office last year, his administration has taken an aggressive stance against major news outlets, including limiting access to the Oval Office and other restricted spaces.
As pool coverage resumed for Xi's arrival at the White House on Friday, Trump declined to answer questions from reporters on China and Iran, his media ban and a controversial new taxpayer-funded TV ad that promotes his presidency. He later thanked reporters.
"We appreciate the fair coverage. It's been very fair. We appreciate it," Trump later told reporters alongside Xi.
The White House did not respond to a request for comment about the restored press access.
UNPRECEDENTED CAMPAIGN
Trump banned the three news outlets from the White House complex over coverage he asserted was false or negative. Their access was reinstated on Thursday, after a federal judge deemed the ban likely unconstitutional and ordered their access to be immediately restored.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organisations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the action.
Despite the temporary ruling restoring access, the court has not yet resolved the main challenge to the ban, based on the First Amendment of the US Constitution that protects the right to free speech and a free press. The news outlets now have until Sept 28 to ask the judge to keep their access in place while the case moves forward.
Even if the outlets won a permanent injunction against the ban, Trump could still pursue his case in federal court.
Trump has waged an unprecedented campaign against the media since returning to office last year, launching personal attacks on journalists, denying access to some outlets and suing news organisations, as well as calling on ⁠the Federal Communications Commission to strip broadcast stations of their licenses.
FRIENDLIEST PRESS CORPS
On Thursday, Trump made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about China – which imposes strict censorship across its media – having the friendliest press corps, as he welcomed Xi to the White House.
While the White House on Thursday told the court it had reinstated CNN, MS NOW and Politico's access, CNN and MS NOW later said some of their journalists were denied access to cover Xi's arrival for the White House state dinner, according to the Washington Post.
A lawyer for the three outlets in court this week warned that the White House could again try to revoke the outlets' White House access as the current litigation continues.
David Ellison, CEO of Paramount Skydance, which is seeking to merge with CNN-parent Warner Bros. Discovery, attended the Trump-Xi state dinner Thursday night.
Critics have raised concerns about Paramount-owned CBS News tailoring coverage to favour Trump, although Ellison has promised to create an editorial independence board for both CBS and CNN as part of the deal.--REUTERS

Title: Pairin Kitingan: Mother tongues risk fading when no longer spoken at home
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Mother tongues risk fading when they are no longer regularly heard and spoken, particularly at home.
Kadazandusun Cultural Association president Tan Sri Joseph Pairin Kitingan said this is a risk he knew from personal experience.
Recalling his childhood, Pairin said he was separated from his parents at 10 and lived in a school hostel in Tawau, where about 90 per cent of the boarders spoke Hakka.
"So, every day I heard Hakka. Eventually, I could speak Hakka.
"But because I had no one around me speaking my mother tongue, I almost forgot it," he said when met after officiating the Borneo Cultural & Heritage Corner (BCHC) in conjunction with the Kota Kinabalu International Book Fair 2026 at the Sabah International Convention Centre here.
Pairin, the Huguan Siou or paramount leader of the Kadazandusun community, said that after becoming involved in community activities, returning to his village and visiting other districts, he began hearing local languages being spoken again.
Gradually, his command of the languages improved, and he can now speak Tambunan and Penampang, as well as some Lotud and Murut.
[[nid:1541367]]
"Every language is at risk of disappearing over time if it is simply left alone, if nothing is done, if it is not spoken or written, especially if parents do not speak their respective languages at home.
"If there is nothing to hear, nothing goes into the mind, nothing is kept in the heart and nothing comes out in writing," he said.
He said communities needed to value the languages inherited from their ancestors and continue writing, recording and sharing them.
"Otherwise, eventually it will disappear. It will no longer be heard," he said.
At the event, Pairin also launched 25 children's books in Kadazandusun.
The books were produced through a collaboration between the Kadazandusun Language Department of Institut Pendidikan Guru (IPG) Kampus Kent, Tuaran, and the Kadazandusun Language Foundation (KLF), with the involvement of students from the Bachelor of Teaching Degree Programme (PISMP) in Kadazandusun Language under the guidance of their lecturers.
Asked whether children's books could help preserve the language, Pairin said: "I think it will definitely help."
Pairin said awareness of mother tongues was beginning to grow, including through writing, publishing and education.
"I think our awareness has begun to grow. That is why our language is now being written, published and incorporated into the school curriculum," he said.
However, he said the foundation for keeping a mother tongue alive still began at home.
"Language must be spoken at home, as the first school," he said.

Title: TikTok pays Alabama US$100m to avoid trial over teen safety
Article:
WASHINGTON: TikTok on Friday agreed to pay Alabama at least US$100 million and enact limits for teen users, avoiding a trial set to begin next week in the southern US state over claims related to child safety on the platform.
"Under the settlement, Alabama will receive a minimum of US$100 million, due to the state within 45 days, with the potential to receive up to US$300 million if certain conditions are met," the office of the Attorney General Steve Marshall said.
The trial had been set to begin on Monday with jury selection.
According to Marshall, TikTok has agreed to enact two-hour daily time limits and restrict access for children from midnight to 6am, among a host of other parental and other safety features.
Alabama's suit was the latest in a wave of litigation targeting social media companies across the United States over the harm their apps allegedly cause young users.
TikTok had also previously settled cases against it that were headed for trial, including a Los Angeles lawsuit brought by a young woman and a suit from a Kentucky school district.
Meta, by contrast, has taken its chances in court – with bruising results.
In March, a jury in New Mexico ordered the Facebook and Instagram owner to pay US$375 million after finding it had misled the public about the safety of its platforms for children.
That same month, a Los Angeles jury found Meta and Google's YouTube negligent in the case of a 20-year-old woman who said she became hooked on social media as a child, awarding her US$6 million.
In August, Meta agreed to pay US$18 billion to settle a sweeping lawsuit brought by US states accusing it of designing Instagram and Facebook to addict children.
Going to trial would have exposed TikTok to unprecedented public scrutiny of how it handles safety internally, with company documents and executive testimony potentially aired in open court.
Alabama originally sued TikTok and its Chinese parent company ByteDance in April 2025, alleging the app was engineered to hook young users "just like a sophisticated gambling machine."
The state later narrowed its case to claims under Alabama's Deceptive Trade Practices Act, focusing on whether TikTok misrepresented the effectiveness of features such as "Restricted Mode" and "Kids Mode."
In its complaint, the state said investigators set up TikTok accounts posing as 13-, 14- and 15-year-olds in Alabama and switched on Restricted Mode.
Despite TikTok's assurances that users in that mode should not see mature themes, the accounts were quickly served videos about suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, alcohol and sex, according to the filing.
The state also accused TikTok of falsely telling app stores the platform was suitable for children aged 12 and up and contained only mild or infrequent mature content.
TikTok, whose US operations were transferred this year to a venture led by American investors, has argued that the case should be paused and that it is shielded by Section 230, a federal law that protects online platforms from liability for content posted by users.
Asked for comment on the settlement Friday, a TikTok spokesperson said the company's "priority has always been fostering a safe and positive space where people can be creative, discover what they love, and connect with their community."
"This builds on our commitment and core objective to continually enhance our robust safety tools to protect teens," the spokesperson added.--AFP

Title: Elderly woman loses RM80k in 'ghost money aid' scam
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 73-year-old woman lost RM80,000 after falling victim to a scam offering fake "ghost money aid".
Kuala Terengganu district police chief, Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor, said the housewife lodged a police report at 4.17pm yesterday.
He said the incident began last year when the victim, who was at home, became interested in obtaining "ghost money aid" advertised online through Facebook.
She then communicated via WhatsApp with a person using the name "Ustaz Nasihin" through a telephone number provided.
"The person offered 'ghost money aid', purportedly for home repairs, settling debts and making donations to orphans.
"To obtain the aid, the victim was required to make payments in advance according to the amount instructed," he said.
Azli said the person later informed the victim that the money had been deposited into her account.
However, he said the victim checked her account and found that no money had been deposited as promised.
He said on Sept 24, the victim was contacted by a person who introduced himself as "Vee Hong" and claimed to be holding the money.
"Vee Hong told the victim that the money could be collected, but she first had to make a RM50,000 payment as a fine because the money had not been collected on time.
"The victim then contacted 'Ustaz Nasihin' for an explanation and was told that he had been detained and fined RM50,000.
"The person asked the victim to make the payment, promising that the money would be returned," he said.
Azli said after being deceived, the victim made 13 transactions to a bank account, amounting to RM80,000.
He said all the money came from the victim's savings and the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly fisherman's body found on Melaka beach
Article:
MELAKA: The body of an elderly fisherman was found lying face down along the beach near Jalan Residen, Padang Temu, here yesterday.
Melaka Tengah district police chief, Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas, said police received information about the discovery through the MERS 999 emergency line at 11.13am.
He said a man reported finding the body near the beach opposite 8 Residence, Jalan Residen, Taman Padang Temu.
"Police found the victim, a 74-year-old man identified as Mohammad Chalip.
"Investigations found that the victim was a fisherman from Sungai Duyong jetty and was known among fishermen in the area," he said in a statement.
Halim said based on the account of an 8 Residence security guard, the witness saw an unattended fishing boat while conducting a patrol at about 10.30am.
"The witness continued the patrol before spotting the victim lying face down along the beach.
"The victim's son said his father left home at about 7am for the jetty to carry out his daily routine of fishing at sea.
"The witness also said the victim suffered from high blood pressure.
"The case has been classified as sudden death, and the body was claimed by family members for burial," he said.

Title: Anwar denies trying to interfere in Negri Sembilan royal crisis
Article:
PENDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied trying to interfere in the Negri Sembilan royal crisis.
He said he was defending the constitutional monarchy system practised in the country.
Anwar said he did not want action by the Undangs in the state to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar too easily, as this could lead to a wider crisis for the constitutional monarchy system.
He said the Negri Sembilan laws stipulated that a change could only be made on specific grounds, including if the Yang di-Pertuan Besar became mentally incapacitated, lost his sight or speech, became disqualified under Islamic law, committed an act detrimental to the dignity of the office or deliberately disregarded the state constitution.
"That is why the Attorney-General took a firm decision that we cannot make it easy to remove a ruler.
"Imagine if this starts there. Tomorrow, the prime minister and cabinet might think they want to replace the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, and write to the Malay rulers saying they do not agree with the Agong.
"That cannot be done. It is not the prime minister's power to decide to replace the Agong. The prime minister is the chief executive who administers the country and there are limits to his powers. He cannot amend the Constitution on matters concerning Islam, the Malay language, Malay special rights and the institution of the rulers," he said.
He said this when speaking at the Sebarkan Salam and Pendang Berselawat programme at Pondok Mujamma' Ibn Sunni Al-Talaqqi here last night.
Also present was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
Anwar said he was prepared to take a firm position in defending the Malay rulers to ensure the constitutional monarchy continued alongside the executive branch of government.
He said he was also confident that the people, particularly Malays, as well as Chinese and Indians, would support the existing system to ensure the country's stability.
"It is not as if he has just become the Yang di-Pertuan Besar. After so many years, suddenly there is a move to remove him.
"That is the Undangs' decision, but I said, discuss it properly.
"I do not agree. You cannot simply remove a ruler. The constitutional monarchy system does not work that way.
"The ruler should not be slighted. If there is a problem or disagreement, I would seek an audience and express my views.
"You cannot remove a ruler. If a ruler can be removed so easily, the royal institution will disappear from this country," he said.
On Wednesday, Anwar described the action by Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and the state executive council to remove Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as "rude" and "uncivilised".
Ismail had earlier confirmed that the proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar was unanimously decided and endorsed by the state executive council. Reports at the time said the state executive council took that position, while the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang later reiterated that Tuanku Muhriz remained the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

Title: Student death prompts calls for transparent probe, stern action
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The death of a Form Two student  in Kuala Pilah has prompted calls for a thorough investigation into alleged bullying.
The student was found unconscious at the school hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN), where he was pronounced dead.
Former Education Minister Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin, in a post on Threads, conveyed his condolences to the student's family and urged the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation without compromise.
"The authorities must investigate this case transparently and thoroughly over allegations that the victim was bullied to ensure justice for the deceased and his family," he said.
Echoing the call, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman and Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki also expressed his condolences and described bullying in educational institutions as an issue that could not be compromised.
He urged the authorities and Education Ministry to take swift and firm action against anyone found to be involved.
Earlier, posts on social media claimed that a Form Two student, had died yesterday, with family members alleging that the victim had been assaulted while at the school hostel.
The matter was shared by a woman who claimed to be the victim's aunt in several posts on Threads since last night.
According to the woman, she was informed of her nephew's death after receiving a call from her sibling, who was also the victim's mother.
In subsequent posts, she claimed that the victim's remains were initially at Kuala Pilah Hospital before being taken to a hospital in Seremban for a post-mortem.

Title: Serian records unhealthy API reading
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Serian recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 154 as of 7am today.
Based on the latest data from the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 63 other areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings.
In Sarawak, Sri Aman recorded an API reading of 97, followed by Kuching (95), Bintulu (92), Samarahan (89), Sarikei (81) and Sibu (71).
In Sabah, the monitoring station at Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded an API reading of 84, while Tawau and Sandakan recorded 78 and 72 respectively.
In Johor, Pasir Gudang recorded an API reading of 83, while Larkin recorded 81.
Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded a reading of 82.
Batu Pahat in Johor and Sungai Petani in Kedah each recorded an API reading of 81.
API readings from 0 to 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate and 101 to 200 as unhealthy.

Title: Form Two student dies after alleged bullying at school hostel
Article:
KUALA PILAH: A Form Two student at a school in the district died last night, reportedly after being bullied at the school hostel.
The 14-year-old was reportedly found unconscious at the school hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN), where he was pronounced dead.
The body was taken to the Forensic Medicine Department at Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital, Seremban, for a post-mortem.
Meanwhile, Kuala Pilah district police chief, Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin, confirmed the incident and said further details would be provided soon.

Title: Trump warns Xi against Iran support as Beijing pledges no assistance
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump warned Chinese President Xi Jinping against providing support to Iran during talks in Washington this week and received assurances that China would not do so, the US ambassador to China said on Friday.
The warning came amid reports that China had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired air-defence missile launchers and that Teheran had found ways to evade sanctions on its oil sales with Chinese help.
David Perdue, Trump's ambassador to Beijing, said in a CNBC interview that Trump reiterated to Xi that direct or indirect support for Iran was "totally unacceptable."
Asked separately on Fox News if that meant China would stop assisting Iran, Perdue said Washington received assurances from Beijing on Thursday.
"We've seen movement ... on that already. That's what the commitment is. They assured us yesterday they're not doing that," Perdue told Fox News' "America's Newsroom" programme.
Trump later on Friday acknowledged that the two leaders discussed the war that the US and Israel launched on Iran in late February, without giving details.
MISSILE LAUNCHERS, SANCTIONS DODGE
US lawmakers had urged Trump to confront Xi over reports of Chinese assistance to Iran, raising concerns that Chinese entities may have given targeting help that led to US casualties in the conflict.
Chinese officials have assured Iran that even after the Trump-Xi meeting China will not limit its economic, political or military ties with Teheran under pressure from the US president, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.
Reuters reported in July that Iran was expected to receive within weeks a first shipment out of up to 400 Chinese-made shoulder-fired air-defence missile launchers.
Iran has also used a barter-like arrangement to bypass sanctions on its oil sales and buy billions of dollars' worth of goods from China, including military gear, two senior Iranian sources and three other people familiar with the matter told Reuters earlier this month.
Chinese state newswire Xinhua reported on Thursday that Xi had urged the US and Iran to return to negotiations to end the war, but Xi has not publicly commented on Chinese support for Iran.
Trump and Xi did not take formal questions during the three-day state visit to Washington.
Earlier this month, Trump brushed aside a report ​that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July.
"They basically do what we do," Trump ​told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sept 13. "When they say China spies on us, I say ​you're right and we spy on them too."--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Storm leaves Klang Valley roads clogged, hawker stalls wrecked
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists faced heavy rain, fallen trees and severe traffic congestion across parts of the Klang Valley yesterday, with several roads blocked by fallen trees.
Photos and videos shared on Threads showed road users stranded as branches and tree trunks blocked lanes along the North Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) near Jalan Duta-Bukit Lanjan and in Damansara Damai.
One user, ayranajihabtmuhdherry, said
traffic had been reduced
to a single lane.
"The traffic is terrible, with only one lane passable. The rain wasn't even heavy earlier," the user wrote.
Meanwhile, a takoyaki seller in Damansara Damai
apologised to customers
after cancelling orders due to the weather.
"I'm sorry to all Empire Tako customers. I had to cancel the orders. The weather is really bad today. Please pray that we can resume business," the seller wrote.
Banana fritter seller hafiezrin also said he was
forced to close his stall
for two days after it and nearby hawker tents were damaged.

His post drew encouragement from other users, with one writing: "Come back stronger. We'll buy your banana fritters later."

"Salute to Malaysians, especially the riders who immediately stopped to help move the tree," the user wrote.
Another user, mohdazhar.anuar, thanked those
who helped clear fallen trees
along the North-South Expressway northbound route between Jalan Duta and Bukit Lanjan.

a motorist was also assisted

Title: Beyond bigger pay cheques, what can keep Malaysia's frontline workers from Singapore? [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For Malaysian workers weighing whether to stay in Malaysia or cross the Causeway for a bigger pay cheque, the dilemma goes beyond Singapore's higher salaries.
Experts told Business Times that the decision also comes down to career prospects, with many workers in Malaysia struggling to see how their wages can rise meaningfully as they gain skills, experience and greater responsibilities.
The issue is particularly acute among frontline workers, many of whom are drawn to better-paying jobs across the southern border while local salaries remain clustered around the RM1,700 minimum wage.
Singapore remains the largest destination for Malaysians working abroad, according to the Statistics Department.
Its International Migration Statistics, Malaysia, 2025 report incorporates findings from a 2022 study of Malaysians working in Singapore.
The study found that 39 per cent of Malaysians working in the city-state were skilled workers, 35 per cent semi-skilled and 26 per cent low-skilled.
Among low-skilled workers, a category that includes some frontline occupations, 40 per cent earned between S$1,500 and S$2,199 a month, while another 34 per cent earned between S$2,200 and S$3,599.
Back home, low-skilled workers earned an average of RM2,128 a month in 2024, with a median salary of RM1,654, according to the Statistics Department.
For Malaysia, experts said the challenge is not only to raise the wage floor, but also to create clearer wage progression so workers have a stronger incentive to build their careers locally.
THE CAUSEWAY WAGE GAP
Khazanah Research Institute research associate Wan Amirah Wan Usamah said Singapore's higher wages reflected not only productivity but also deliberate policies to raise workers' pay.
In Singapore, the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) links wages to job levels, skills, training and career progression.
The system distinguishes between local workers covered by the PWM and those outside its scope. Local workers refer to Singapore citizens and permanent residents.
Firms employing foreign workers must comply with PWM wage requirements for covered local employees and pay those outside its scope at least the Local Qualifying Salary.
For Malaysia, Amirah said the RM1,700 minimum wage, implemented on Feb 1, 2025, remained an important wage floor but did not address the problem of workers remaining close to that level for years.
"Malaysia should not wait for productivity to rise before raising wages. Rather, wage growth and productivity growth should be pursued together," she said.
She said higher wages could themselves support productivity by improving worker retention, encouraging investment in skills and giving employers greater incentive to upgrade technology and work processes.
[[nid:1541336]]
WAGE PROGRESSION MATTERS
Jobstreet by SEEK Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam said advertised salaries showed considerable variation among frontline jobs, highlighting the need for clearer wage progression.
Its first-half 2026 data put median monthly advertised salary ranges at RM1,700 to RM2,000 for cleaners, RM1,900 to RM2,500 for security workers, RM2,000 to RM2,500 for food and beverage (F&B) workers and RM1,800 to RM2,300 for retail workers.
About 62 per cent of cleaning advertisements had a minimum advertised salary at or below RM1,700, compared with 43 per cent for retail, 39 per cent for security and 17 per cent for F&B.
Candidate salary expectations also exceeded advertised starting pay by an average of 35 per cent for cleaning, 33 per cent for F&B, 53 per cent for security and seven per cent for retail.
Lam said the data underscored the importance of creating opportunities for workers to earn more as they gained experience, rather than relying solely on higher entry-level wages.
Across the frontline roles analysed, the median advertised minimum salary for experienced positions was around 23 per cent higher than for junior positions, while the upper end of salary ranges was about 25 per cent higher.
However, the degree of progression varied sharply.
Advertised salaries for experienced warehouse and manufacturing positions were around 40 to 44 per cent higher than junior levels, while cleaning, hospitality and retail showed little differentiation.
"A well-designed wage ladder can give employers a more structured way to recognise greater skills, experience and responsibility over time, while giving workers clearer visibility of how their earning potential can grow," Lam said.
He added that a structured wage ladder could be more sustainable than blanket wage increases because it linked higher pay to workers' skills, experience and contributions.
THE COST CHALLENGE FOR SMEs
But narrowing the wage gap with Singapore is no straightforward task for Malaysian employers, particularly smaller businesses already grappling with rising operating costs.
SME Association president Dr Chin Chee Seong cautioned that efforts to raise wages must take account of the wider cost pressures facing businesses.
He said many small and medium enterprises (SMEs) already paid above RM1,700 to attract and retain workers with the required skills and experience, although their ability to absorb further increases varied by industry and business size.
Moving quickly towards the RM3,100 living-wage benchmark could also have implications beyond employees currently earning RM1,700, he said.
"If the salary at the lower level is increased significantly, those earning above it will naturally expect their salaries to be adjusted as well to reflect their experience, skills, responsibilities and seniority," he said.
Chin said this wage compression effect meant a substantial increase at the bottom could raise payroll costs across an entire organisation, particularly for labour-intensive SMEs operating on thin margins.
The RM3,100 benchmark is used under the Government-linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP), taking into account industry wages and cost-of-living standards in the Belanjawanku 2024/2025 expenditure guide.
The latest GEAR-uP progress report showed that 91.7 per cent, or 189,817 of 206,987 directly employed Malaysian workers in government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies, earned at least RM3,100 a month.
BUILDING CLEARER WAGE PATHS
Amirah said Malaysia could draw lessons from Singapore's approach without replicating its wage model wholesale.
"Malaysia should take the principle of structured progression, rather than the precise Singaporean framework," she said.
Lam said employers also needed to look beyond salaries when making frontline jobs more attractive.
"Working hours, physical demands, location, working environment and opportunities for progression can all form part of the overall proposition," he said.
For SMEs, Chin said government support would be crucial if Malaysia moved towards a more structured progressive-wage system.
This could include co-funding of wage increases, grants, tax incentives and affordable financing for automation, digitalisation and training.
Such measures would help labour-intensive SMEs absorb higher payroll costs while improving productivity and creating room for further wage increases, he said.

Title: Pentagon wins court battle to exclude Anthropic from AI supply chain
Article:
WASHINGTON: A US appeals court upheld on Friday the Pentagon's decision to exclude Anthropic from its supply chain, a decision taken when the AI startup refused to remove certain safeguards on its Claude model.
The conflict began in February when Anthropic refused Pentagon Secretary Pete Hegseth's demand to remove restrictions on the use of Claude for fully autonomous lethal weapons and mass domestic surveillance of Americans.
The supply chain risk designation, formally made in March, canceled Anthropic's military contracts and barred other Pentagon contractors from using its technology.
The military had been using Claude across a range of classified and sensitive systems.
According to the decision, an Anthropic executive had questioned the use of Claude by a Pentagon contractor, Palantir, during the military operation that captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on Jan 3.
This objection "led to alarm" and "raised material doubts as to whether they would cause their software to stop working or cause some other disastrous action that would put our warfighters['] lives in danger," according to Under Secretary of Defense Emil Michael, as quoted in the opinion.
Anthropic insists it cannot modify its models once delivered to the military.
But the company determines the behavior of each new version, and the military must keep up to date on the latest offerings, the Washington appeals court found.
In his opinion Judge Gregory Katsas, writing for two of the three appellate judges, said "in our Republic, it is the President and the Secretary of War who must determine how best to balance" risks.
- 'HAMMER OF JUSTICE' -
The designation against Anthropic marked a highly unusual application of the authority against a US company.
The Pentagon immediately turned to its competitors.
Its major rival OpenAI, creator of ChatGPT, signed an agreement on the same day as Anthropic's ban, while xAI, Elon Musk's company that develops Grok, signed in February and Google and Microsoft a few months later.
Anthropic has since become a pariah at the White House, even as it plays a major role in the highly crucial AI sector and, valued at nearly one trillion dollars, heads for a blockbuster IPO expected in weeks.
The White House has also bristled at Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's repeated warnings about the dangers of AI – with US President Donald Trump calling them a hoax.
Michael celebrated the ruling on X, writing: "The hammer of justice has smashed Anthropic arguments."
"Warfighters will sleep better knowing that no private company will insert their opinions in the chain of command."
The appeals court decision conflicted with a separate federal court decision in California that found last month that a broader ban imposed by the Trump administration against Anthropic was illegal.
The Pentagon decision upheld on Friday was based on public procurement regulations and now remains in effect.
"We respectfully disagree with the court's decision. Another federal court has already held the government's parallel designation unlawful. We remain confident in our position and are considering all options, including further review," an Anthropic spokesperson said in a statement to US media.--AFP

Title: Lula bans online sports betting days before Brazil election
Article:
SAO PAULO: Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Friday banned sports betting sites, the biggest sponsor of the country's football clubs, just days before a nailbiter election in which he is seeking a fourth term.
Gambling has exploded in Brazil in recent years, dragging many into debt, and opinion polls show strong voter opposition to the industry, which Lula has labeled a "cancer."
"It is no longer possible to deposit money into betting sites in the country," said Finance Minister Dario Durigan, announcing the ban at an event alongside Lula.
The initiative is the latest in a flurry of moves made by Lula before a first round of voting on Oct 4, as he stands neck-and-neck with right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in the polls.
Brazil's betting market has boomed since a regulatory framework was established in 2023, accompanied by aggressive advertising both on the streets and online from influencers and sports stars.
Thirteen of the country's 20 first division football clubs have an online betting site as their main shirt sponsor. And soccer stars like Neymar and Vinicius Junior are among the most prominent faces in advertising for the industry.
According to a government statement, 85 licenses have been granted for betting, each valued at 30 million reais (US$5.7 million), which will not be refunded.
Durigan said that new advertising contracts for betting companies were also immediately banned, while current contracts would be void after Oct 6.
As of that date, there will be no "site, no application and no legal sponsorship of bets in the country," he said.
Powerhouse football club Flamengo called the move a "heavy blow to Brazilian sports," warning it could impact not only professional football, but youth academies, women's soccer, Olympic sports and various championships.
"Brazil spent years debating how to regulate sports betting," the club said in a statement. "One cannot establish a rule, induce companies and institutions to make commitments based on it, and then, overnight, overhaul the entire regulatory framework."
- BOLSONARO SLAMS 'DESPERATE' LULA -
Durigan said the government had attempted to regulate the industry, but it had become a public health issue, with more than 60 billion reais (US$11 billion) flowing from families to legal betting companies.
"I spoke with a young guy who tried to kill himself three times" over his gambling addiction, said Lula after signing a provisional measure enforcing the ban.
"I decided to take a necessary, tough, and drastic measure. It's like cancer," he said. "Either we remove the tumour, or it kills us."
The measure will, however, require approval by Congress to become law.
Bolsonaro slammed the move in a statement earlier Friday.
"President Lula is desperate," said Bolsonaro, describing the move as another "populist, hypocritical, and election-driven" measure on the eve of the polls.
Several soccer clubs have expressed opposition to the ban, arguing that betting sponsors are vital to their financial health.
Lula said this argument is "nonsense" and called for an end to the "shamelessness in soccer."
The National Association of Games and Lotteries (ANJL), which represents licensed betting operators, joined eight other industry groups Thursday in warning that prohibition could drive gamblers toward illegal platforms.
It also highlighted a loss in tax revenue and jobs.
In 2025, the sector paid 9.95 billion reais (US$1.73 billion) in taxes to the federal government.
"The challenges are real. The answer lies in oversight and stronger regulation," said the ANJL in a statement. "To regulate is to control. To ban is to lose control.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Children caught in porn web, murders among major crimes this week [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The arrest of eight children in a police operation, which also uncovered more than 2.1 million child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and pornography files, was among some of the major crimes reported this week.
The police operation,
codenamed Op Pedo 3.0,
exposed the disturbing production and sale of CSAM-related videos and animations through closed online groups for between RM50 and RM60.
The arrests prompted Suhakam's Children's Commissioner to call for a child-sensitive approach, saying minors involved in CSAM cases should be assessed separately from adult perpetrators and exploiters, with rehabilitation prioritised where appropriate.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) received 12,529 applications to take down pornographic and CSAM content on social media and messaging services between Jan 1 and Sept 21.  Of these, 11,665 pieces of content were taken down and 1,031 websites shut down.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC would continue strengthening its technical and forensic cooperation with police to track those misusing network services to sexually exploit children online.
Below are some of the crimes reported this week.
CONVENIENCE STORES ATTACKED WITH EXPLOSIVES
In Kuching, Sarawak, two men were detained on suspicion of carrying out arson attacks on two 24-hour convenience stores using explosives.
The suspects, aged 40 and 23,
have been remanded
until Sept 26.
In the first incident at King Centre, a commercial and mixed-development hub, firecrackers were used. There were no reports of losses. The second incident along Jalan Green caused a fire. The men allegedly arrived at the premises and threw an object inside, causing two explosions and the fire.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the two attacks involved a similar modus operandi, with masked men in dark clothing throwing objects believed to contain explosive or flammable materials into the premises.
Police examined CCTV footage and analysed materials recovered from the scenes to determine whether the incidents were connected.
Investigators were also looking into allegations that the outlets were selling online gambling top-ups, with authorities considering possible action against their business licences if the claims were substantiated.
FIVE HELD OVER MYANMAR'S  MURDER
Five men were arrested in Kota Baru, Kelantan, over the murder of a 18-year-old Myanmar refugee.
The victim was found lying unconscious with a slash wound to his neck at a workers' dormitory near a Muslim cemetery in Taman Desa Kujid, Panji.
Police found a parang believed to be the murder weapon and arrested five suspects - a Malaysian and four Myanmar refugees.
They also seized a Mitsubishi Triton and four mobile phones while police continue the probe to ascertain the motive for the murder.
THREE FOREIGN STUDENTS IN MURDER PROBE
In Ipoh, Perak, police arrested three foreign students to assist in an investigation into the death of a 53-year-old man in Kampung Kuchai.
Police said the victim was discovered by members of the public in an open area in Kampung Kuchai with facial injuries.
He was rushed to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital, where he received treatment for several days before being pronounced dead on Sept 22.
In follow-up operations, police arrested
three private university students,
aged 17 to 20, at their homes in Ipoh to facilitate the investigations.
Post-mortem checks found that the cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head. Police are investigating the relationship between the victim and the three suspects, as well as the motive for the  attack.
MAN, SON ARRESTED FOR DISABLED WOMAN'S MURDER
In Kuala Kangsar, Perak, a 49-year-old disabled woman was found dead at her home in Kampung Cheh Hilir. Her husband and their 15-year-old son were detained to facilitate investigations.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the incident
stemmed from a misunderstanding
between the victim and the suspects.
The victim, who lived with her husband and three children, was found lying face down and unconscious in the living room, covered in blood and suffering from stab wounds.
Her 44-year-old husband reportedly heard her calling for help after she complained that someone had stabbed her leg with a sharp object beneath their wooden house.
Villagers later helped search for the couple's 15-year-old son, who was found hiding in an oil palm plantation. Police also seized a knife believed to have been used in the incident at the scene.

Title: Rais charged with sedition, Najib back in court after conditional pardon [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Dewan Negara president Tan Sri Rais Yatim was charged with sedition in relation to the current Negri Sembilan constitutional crisis.
The 84-year-old was accused of uttering seditious statements relating to Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar being made the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
There were also interesting developments this week with
Datuk Seri Najib Razak returning to court
after the Pardons Board's decision allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence at home.
Then there was former Tabung Haji chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani who was charged with four counts of accepting over RM300,000 in house renovation costs.
Below are the major court cases this week.
RAIS CHARGED WITH SEDITION IN RELATION to NEGRI CONSTITUTIONAL CRISIS
In Melaka,
Rais, who is also Parti Wawasan Negara chairman
pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court to a charge under the Sedition Act.
The veteran politician who had been vocal about the Negri Sembilan constitutional dispute, became the first person to be charged with sedition in connection with crisis.
The 84-year-old former Jelebu member of parliament pleaded not guilty to a charge of allegedly uttering seditious words relating to the proclamation of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri  Sembilan.
The charge, framed under paragraph 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948 and punishable under subsection 4(1), carries a fine of up to RM5,000, a maximum jail term of three years, or both upon conviction.
Rais was granted RM8,000 bail with one surety and will return to court on Oct 27 for mention.
NAJIB APPLIES FOR STAY IN 1MDB CASE
Najib, 73, was in court
seeking a stay of execution of his 15-year jail sentence
and RM11.38 billion fine in the RM2.28 billion 1Malaysia Development Berhad case. The application will be heard on Oct 14.
Najib is appealing against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering.
His 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case was ordered to begin after he completes his current sentence in the SRC International case.
FORMER TABUNG HAJI COO BACK IN COURT
Former Tabung Haji chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani was charged with four counts of accepting over RM300,000 in house renovation costs.
Adi Azuan was accused of accepting more than
RM302,000 in renovation costs
for four houses in 2017.
The 56-year-old, who retired from Tabung Haji in 2025, allegedly accepted the bribes while serving as a public servant, from AG Reka Sdn Bhd director Thamsulazri Ismail, whom he knew had a connection with his official duties.
The father of four was allowed a RM50,000 bail with two sureties and is set to return to court on Nov 25 for mention.
PROSECUTION FILES APPEAL IN BANDAR UTAMA SCHOOL MURDER
The Bandar Utama school murder case remained in the spotlight after Shah Alam High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid released her 77-page grounds of judgment.
It revealed how she came to her decision to acquit a
15-year-old boy accused of killing
his 16-year-old schoolmate, who suffered 180 to 200 stab wounds in a Bandar Utama girls toilet on Oct 14 last year.
Adlin found that the teenager was suffering from
severe early-onset schizophrenia
and was of unsound mind when the incident occurred.
She said the evidence showed symptoms had been present from a young age but had gone unrecognised and untreated for five years.
She said Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta director and consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony had diagnosed the boy with schizophrenia, of very early onset (before the age of 13) with psychopathic and sadistic traits.
The prosecution has since appealed to the Court of Appeal against the acquittal.
ANWAR SETTLES DEFAMATION SUIT
A case management at the High Court for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's 2023
defamation suit against Pendang MP
Datuk Awang Solahuddin Hashim turned into a settlement when both parties reached an amicable resolution.
Anwar and Awang Solahuddin said they had decided to resolve the dispute after considering the litigation costs to be incurred by both sides.
They also said there were matters of greater importance and deserving of priority in the interests of the people and the country.
As part of the settlement, Awang Solahuddin agreed to withdraw the statements that formed the basis of the suit and not to repeat or republish them.
Anwar, meanwhile, agreed to withdraw the suit without an order as to costs and without liberty to file a fresh action in relation to the same matter.
Awang Solahuddin had claimed that Anwar was more vindictive than former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
In turn, Anwar contended that the remarks were malicious, untrue, defamatory and slanderous.

Title: Trump took Xi on ballroom tour: White House
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump took Chinese President Xi Jinping and other state dinner guests on a tour of the construction site of his new ballroom, the White House said Friday.
Trump suddenly announced that he was "going off" during Thursday's banquet and wanted to show off the US$400 million project being built next door.
"As a special treat in honour of President Xi and Madam Peng, I'd like to invite everyone in the room to visit through that beautiful curtain in the back," Trump told guests.
"It's one year away from completion of the new ballroom that you've heard about, and you will see something that I think you will really love."
Journalists were then led out of the dinner, but a White House official told AFP they "can confirm they took a tour," when asked if Trump had later taken Xi and other guests to see the ballroom.
The New York Post reported that access involved stepping out of the doors of the East Room where the dinner took place, then walking along a red carpet to a stand where they could inspect the ballroom site.
Guests at the dinner also included top tech CEOs such as Tesla's Elon Musk and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg.
The tour of one of the most sensitive US government sites underscored Trump's efforts to impress Xi on a lavish state visit aimed at smoothing tensions between the two superpowers.
Trump has previously dubbed it the "greatest military-complex-slash-ballroom anywhere in the world" because it will have six floors of sensitive underground sites and a drone port on the roof.
He has repeatedly invoked national security to bat away questions about planning permission and the cost of the ballroom and other sites.
The US president had earlier shown Xi the outside of the ballroom while giving the Chinese president a tour of the new White House helipad, during which he also took Xi aboard his helicopter, Marine One.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump, Xi summit ends with pomp, pandas and few major breakthroughs
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump took Chinese leader Xi Jinping to see the founding documents of American democracy on Friday, capping a state visit full of pomp and pageantry but with no major breakthroughs.
Trump said he discussed the stalled Iran war with Xi, and the two leaders confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at international summits in China and the United States.
But as Trump showed Xi around the National Archives in Washington – home to the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution – it underscored that the summit was more about spectacle than substance.
The summit produced no major policy announcements on flashpoints like artificial intelligence, Taiwan or trade, apart from a two-month extension of a tariff truce between the world's two largest economies.
The only other reveal was that two Chinese pandas would soon arrive at a US zoo.
The message from the US and Chinese sides was that the summit had nevertheless helped smooth tensions between the rival superpowers over a host of issues.
Trump said the meeting was "one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A."
"We've made great strides, very positive for both countries," Trump told reporters as he had tea with Xi at the White House on Friday before the archives trip.
- 'STRATEGIC STABILITY' -
Trump has rolled out the red carpet throughout the visit, treating Xi to a state banquet full of US tech titans, plus military parades, a flyover and even a tour of his new White House helipad and ballroom.
For his part, Xi said his Washington trip had added "new substance" to his summit with Trump in Beijing in May.
The Chinese leader added that they had agreed to "strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity."
The announcement that the two leaders would continue their dialogue was perhaps the biggest deliverable for both sides.
Both leaders confirmed they would meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzen, China, in November and the G20 forum at Trump's Doral resort in Miami in December.
On the final day of the authoritarian Chinese leader's trip, Trump and his wife Melania brought Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan to the imposing National Archives building.
There they inspected the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary this year and which set out the path for American independence from the "tyrant" British king.
Beneath the rotunda, Trump also showed Xi the US constitution, the document that set out the principles of the country's democratic government two and a half centuries ago.
"We're just comparing how this goes 250 years, theirs goes 6,000 years," Trump told reporters, referring to China's ancient roots, as he stood alongside Xi, chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, which has ruled China since 1949.
- IRAN TALKS -
Trump confirmed during the archive visit that the two leaders had discussed the US-Israeli war in Iran, which is approaching its seven-month mark.
The Republican has faced pressure from Democrats and his own party to confront Xi over reports that Beijing has supplied Teheran with intelligence for attacks on US troops.
"We did, we did," Trump said at the National Archives when asked if they had talked about Iran.
Asked if he thought there would be progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which is crucial for the flow of oil, Trump replied: "I think we're going to do great."
Trump's showcasing of US democracy at the National Archives comes a week after he banned three major US media outlets from the White House. They were readmitted on Thursday on the orders of a US judge.
The First Amendment of the US Constitution protects the freedom of the press.
Rights groups criticise China for its lack of press freedoms and the right of free expression.
Trump also publicly mocked his democratically elected predecessor Joe Biden as he gave Xi a tour of the White House on Thursday, showing him a picture of an "autopen" that he has mounted in a gallery of US presidents instead of Biden's portrait.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia calls for Myanmar to fulfil Asean Five-Point Consensus
Article:
NEW YORK: Malaysia has stressed the importance of Myanmar fulfilling its responsibilities as an Asean member and implementing the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) to help address the prolonged crisis in the country.
This was among the positions conveyed by Malaysia during a courtesy call by International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) president Mirjana Spoljaric on Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
According to a meeting note shared with the media, Malaysia will continue to engage constructively with Asean in efforts to address the situation in Myanmar.
"Discussions focused on the increasingly challenging global humanitarian situation, including developments in Myanmar and the need to ensure that humanitarian assistance can continue to reach those in need," the statement read.
During the meeting, the ICRC president also invited Malaysia to be represented by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at the High-Level Conference on Humanitarian Issues in War, which will be held in Jordan on Dec 7 at the invitation of Jordan's King Abdullah II.
The ICRC said participation at the level of a head of state or government would send a strong message about the international community's commitment to humanitarian issues.
The two sides also discussed autonomous weapons systems, which are receiving increasing attention from the international community.
"In this regard, the international community needs to take immediate action to establish international regulations governing autonomous weapons systems, while supporting the ongoing process in Geneva," the statement said.
Mohamad is currently in New York leading the Malaysian delegation to the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China visit opens new investment, trade opportunities, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou has opened new opportunities for Malaysia to tap investment potential and strengthen trade cooperation with China, bringing shared benefits to the people of both countries.
Anwar said the visit also showcased Malaysia's capabilities on the international stage through the country's participation in the WorldSkills Competition and Summit, as well as the Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE).
"My working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou has yielded meaningful results, particularly in tapping investment potential and trade cooperation that will bring shared benefits and prosperity to the people of Malaysia and China," he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar also said Malaysia had conveyed its firm position on the importance of ensuring that developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and technological advancement did not come at the expense of human values.
He said dialogue and cooperation must continue to be strengthened amid global competition and uncertainty to build a fairer and more equitable world.
"In pursuing developments in AI and technological advancement, humanity and values must not be sidelined.
"Amid global competition that is creating uncertainty, we must move forward through dialogue and cooperation to build a fairer and more equitable world," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia-China diplomatic relations were now at their highest level and the momentum should be harnessed to explore opportunities and pioneer new areas of cooperation.
"Malaysia and China should capitalise on this friendship to continue exploring opportunities and pioneering new and more promising areas of cooperation.
"The Madani Diplomacy Tour will continue to be driven for the people and our beloved Malaysia," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Traffic policeman injured after car rams him during road closure
Article:
TUMPAT: A traffic policeman was injured after being hit by a car while controlling traffic at the Kampung Kepulau traffic light intersection in Palekbang yesterday.
Tumpat district police chief ACP Mohd Khairi Shafie said the 22-year-old policeman from the Tumpat Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division (BSPTD) was closing the road from Morak to Palekbang at about 1.25pm.
He said the road closure was to facilitate the passage of Sultan Muhammad V's entourage for Friday prayers and Majlis Jamuan Rakyat held in conjunction with the Sultan's 57th birthday.
"A Proton Saga driven by a 55-year-old woman from Morak is believed to have failed to notice the presence of the policeman before hitting him.
"The policeman fell and suffered minor injuries.
"He was taken to Tumpat Hospital for outpatient treatment, while the car driver was uninjured," he said in a statement today.
Mohd Khairi said the case was being investigated under Section 79(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He said investigations were ongoing, including efforts to obtain dashcam footage or other recordings that could assist the investigation.
"We advise all road users to comply with instructions from policemen carrying out traffic control duties and pay full attention to road conditions, especially during special operations and traffic control, to prevent unwanted incidents," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt reviewing systems to move business applications fully online, says Hannah
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government is reviewing processes and systems to fully transition business applications online, allowing entrepreneurs to avoid spending unnecessary time following up with officers on application status.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said unnecessary procedures would be eliminated to ease the administrative burden on businesses, improve time and cost efficiency and reduce room for corruption.
Speaking at the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) Installation and 34th Anniversary Night, Hannah said the government must also improve its delivery systems if businesses were expected to adapt and improve.
"I may not have the money to put cash in your hands, but I promise to review and cut out corruption, to cut out unnecessary processes so that you can save money and time, and make business easier for everybody. You have enough challenges dealing with online business and global trends," she said here today.
She said practical administrative changes had already been implemented to provide business owners with greater certainty.
For instance, Hannah said eligible Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) business licences could now be renewed for up to three years, with businesses opting for a two-year renewal receiving a five per cent discount, while a three-year renewal came with a 10 per cent discount.
To further encourage the entertainment and events sector in Kuala Lumpur, Hannah said deposits for concerts and local shows had been reduced by 70 per cent.
On the evolving retail landscape, she urged physical retailers to adapt to changing consumer behaviour by transforming malls into community hubs offering dynamic food, cultural and entertainment experiences.
She said giving consumers compelling reasons to visit and stay was crucial, especially as online shopping became increasingly dominant.
Hannah also advised traditional businesses to consider employing younger talent to help with digitalisation, noting that both young people and senior citizens were now active users of e-wallets and online shopping platforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cambodian delegation explores trade, investment ties during Malaysia visit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Cambodian delegation visited Malaysian household convenience store chain KK Super Mart as part of a business engagement aimed at deepening trade and investment ties between the two countries.
The delegation was welcomed by the Malaysia-Cambodia Business Association (MCBA) and Malaysia Chinese Assembly Hall (MCAH) on Sept 24, with discussions also covering potential cooperation in education, healthcare, tourism and business.
In a joint statement, MCBA and MCAH said the meeting focused on strengthening bilateral trade and investment cooperation, including encouraging more Malaysian companies to explore opportunities in Cambodia and facilitating the entry of promising Cambodian products into the Malaysian market.
MCBA founding president Datuk Seri Ricky Yaw said cooperation should extend beyond trade and investment to include education, healthcare, professional services, tourism and human capital development.
He also encouraged more Cambodian families to consider Malaysia as an education destination, while inviting Cambodians to Malaysia for healthcare, tourism and business opportunities.
The delegation was led by Cambodia's Ministry of Commerce Under Secretary of State Nam Lynal, who encouraged Malaysian companies and investors to visit Cambodia to gain first-hand knowledge of its market and investment opportunities.
At KK Super Mart, the delegation gained insights into Malaysia's retail business model, product range and market development, while exploring opportunities for Malaysian brands to expand into Cambodia.
The delegation was later introduced to the Associated Chinese Societies of Commerce Malaysia (Soccom), where it met business representatives to discuss opportunities in trade, investment, education, healthcare, tourism and business development.
Yaw and Soccom president Datuk Seri Dr Robert Lim said closer ties between business groups and companies from both countries could create more practical business opportunities.
Yaw said MCBA would continue working with MCAH, Soccom and other business associations through business missions, trade exhibitions, investment visits, business matching and people-to-people exchanges.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar approves RM2.8mil to repair infrastructure at 14 Islamic institutions in Kedah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM2.8 million allocation this year to repair basic infrastructure at 14 Islamic education institutions in Kedah.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the allocation was aimed at ensuring students could study in a more comfortable and safe environment.
"The government will continue to uphold the eminence of Islam by strengthening Islamic education institutions and fostering the study and understanding of hadith in society," he said in a Facebook post today.
In the same post, Anwar also announced a RM250,000 allocation for hadith-related programmes.
He said both allocations would be coordinated by the Kedah Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister's Department (ICU JPM).
"Hopefully, this effort will benefit the students and continue to cultivate a culture of knowledge in society," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: Rule of law, good governance must guide Negri Sembilan administration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The principles of the rule of law and good governance must be upheld to ensure all administrative actions are taken within the limits of legal powers and provisions, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the recent suspension of Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal highlighted the importance of ensuring that all administrative actions were based on a clear understanding of the relevant powers and legal provisions.
"The Constitutional and State Law Division of the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has affirmed that the Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) has no legal authority to suspend the duties of the two senior officials.
"The legal basis is clear. Article 37 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS) provides that matters concerning the appointment and suspension of these two key positions fall under the jurisdiction of the Public Services Commission and the Judicial and Legal Service Commission respectively," he said in a Facebook post tonight.
He said the legal clarification by the federal government through the A-GC reflected its commitment to upholding good governance, justice and the rule of law.
"No party can act unilaterally beyond the powers and constitutional provisions that have been established.
"In public administration, every power comes with limits and responsibilities. Respecting these limits is fundamental to strengthening institutions and maintaining confidence in our administrative system," he said.
Saifuddin said public officers entrusted with responsibilities must be protected from actions that do not follow the proper legal channels and processes.
"The rule of law is guaranteed. The country's administration remains stable, orderly and grounded in the Constitution and laws.
"The spirit of amanah is an important safeguard in ensuring the integrity of administrative institutions and the public service remains protected from any action taken without lawful authority.
"This is the foundation of a strong administration. Powers are exercised in accordance with the law, institutions are respected and the people's trust remains the priority," he said.
Earlier, media reported that the Negri Sembilan state executive council's special meeting on Tuesday unanimously decided to suspend Mohd Zafir and Muzalmah with immediate effect.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali had been named to perform the duties of the state secretary until a new appointment was made by the Chief Secretary to the Government.
However, Mohd Zafir continued performing his duties as usual after saying he had not received any official letter regarding the suspension. He also complied with the directive from Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to remain in service in Negri Sembilan.

Title: NST Leader: Policing cyberspace for online sexual predators
Article:
Globally, the most infamous paedophile of all time is arguably Jeffrey Epstein, the late American financier with deep connections to the rich, famous and powerful.
Epstein was arrested on July 6, 2019 on charges of sex trafficking of minor girls, some as young as 14, between 2002 and 2005.
Held at a Manhattan jail without bail while awaiting trial, Epstein was sensationally found dead in his cell just over two weeks later, which was ruled a suicide by hanging.
A Federal Bureau of Investigation probe into Epstein's crimes had amassed three million files, including 180,000 images and 2,000 videos, plus government documents, emails and flight logs.
But Epstein is just one of the many paedophiles who had been arrested or jailed in the United States.
Paedophilia was formally recognised in the late 19th century as a "psychological" concept, shifting sexual deviance from moral failing or legal crime into medicine and pathology.
Psychologists think  paedophilia is a congenital or early-stage neurodevelopmental condition, rather than a learned behaviour.   Psychological outlook aside, Malaysia has its own  problems with paedophiles.
While thankfully not of the same scale as in Epstein's case, the problem is serious enough that 53 people, including eight children, were recently arrested during a nationwide operation targeting child sexual abuse material.
Run by the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, Op Pedo has recorded a significant increase in such criminal cases in recent years. Since 2024, 2.1 million files containing child sexual abuse material and pornography have been uncovered.
Paedophilic content is rampant on social media, private online groups and messaging platforms.
The scale is disturbing, but enforcement is seemingly ineffective at stamping it out.   Pre-emptive measures are necessary, like shielding children adept at navigating social media with digital safety education.
Also urgent are measures to counter grooming, sextortion, manipulation and suspicious online communities, while also providing safe reporting avenues.
Warning children not to chat with strangers in the digital world is already rooted, but it's nearly impossible for parents or schools to protect kids from chatting on digital devices.   Clearer guidance and tools are needed to identify risks without excessive surveillance of  children's digital lives.
The Online Safety Act 2025 might just be the legal tool to marshal platforms to prevent the creation, circulation and monetisation of paedophilic material.   Since eight of the 53 suspects in the recent crackdown are children, the investigations must be done with care.
The Malaysian Human Rights Commission articulated that victims' circumstances should be individually assessed — whether the child was groomed, coerced, threatened, blackmailed or exploited.
