Title: Brazil election candidates mount digital armies
Article:
IN a knife-edge election race, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and main rival Flavio Bolsonaro have deployed volunteer digital armies online to spread their messages and battle for voters.
These online campaigns, unprecedented in scale in Brazil, have highlighted the growing role of social media in the country's politics, while also raising questions about compliance with election rules.
"The cavalry has arrived. Come join this army that will change our country's history," urged Gustavo Gayer, a congressman and Bolsonaro ally.
He was promoting "Direta Ja" (Right Wing Now), a platform launched in July that consists of a website and WhatsApp group where supporters receive daily "visual ammunition" to share on their own social media feeds to boost Bolsonaro's campaign.
Ahead of the Oct 4 first-round vote, Flavio Bolsonaro—the son of jailed former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro—is neck-and-neck with leftist Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.
The website contains readymade posts, allowing users to filter content by their preferred social media platform or category.
The largest of these categories, with around 200 items, features "criticism of the PT", Lula's Workers' Party. These include accusations around public security, food prices and allegations of corruption.
A single video highlighting inconsistencies in a statement made by Lula was shared by more than 500 supporters, according to an AFP investigation.
The platform itself reports that the initiative has generated more than 50 million interactions.
Lula has launched his own social media initiative dubbed "Lula's Spokespersons", aimed at boosting voter engagement.
"Let's join the fight via computer and mobile phone," he urged during a live stream with supporters this month.
"If you are part of this army, rest assured: on the 4th, we will win the election."
Through WhatsApp groups, over 140,000 people receive daily missions to share posts promoting Lula's policy proposals or criticise his main opponent.
The goal, explained Guilherme Boulos, secretary-general of the presidency, is to win the battle in an arena traditionally dominated by the right.
"We need the humility to acknowledge this. They often win these online clashes," he said at the launch of the initiative.
"If they can unify their narrative and set the agenda for public debate, so can we."
Arthur Ituassu, a professor of political communication at the private Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, said while the primary focus used to be on securing as much television airtime as possible, today "social media is fundamental".
"Encouraging this kind of mobilisation aims to reach undecided voters, the ones who will ultimately decide the election," he said.
Even smaller candidates are fighting hard online, such as Renan Santos, who is polling in the low single digits but has built a following among younger voters.
Santos launched an app where supporters earn points and compete for rankings by sharing his content.
Currently ranked first on the candidate's leaderboard is Joao Victor, a 25-year-old university student.
"I do this because I want to help bring about change in the country," he said.
AFP attempted to speak with Lula and Bolsonaro's digital activists, but they either did not respond or refused to comment, maintaining that they were "doing nothing wrong".
Both Lula and Bolsonaro filed lawsuits at the Superior Electoral Court complaining about the other's initiative.
They accused one another of trying to circumvent rules and drive negative campaigning in a coordinated manner.
Both campaigns said they were complying with electoral laws.
The cases are still pending.
Nahomi Helena de Santana, an election law attorney, said organised digital mobilisation could be deemed unlawful if there was an "economic advantage" in exchange for posts, or if content contained disinformation or slander.
She said spreading such content via an "organised" network could bring greater punishment.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'A gesture of gratitude': Najib's family thanks public for contributions towards RM50mil fine
Article:
PEKAN: The family of Datuk Seri Najib Razak has expressed appreciation for public contributions towards paying the RM50 million fine imposed on the former prime minister.
Najib's eldest son, Datuk Mohamad Nizar, said the family was grateful for the contributions, which he said showed that his father's services as a former prime minister were still remembered.
He said the contributions were voluntary and no one was forced to donate.
"Therefore, my family and I would like to thank Malaysians who contributed. Logically, they contributed as a way of repaying my father's services," he said.
Mohamad Nizar, who is also Pekan Umno deputy chief, was speaking at a Pekan Umno press conference following the conditional pardon granted to Najib by the Federal Territories Pardons Board.
The conditional pardon allows Najib, 73, to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of the RM50 million fine. The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board at Istana Negara on Sept 18.
Also present was Pekan Umno chief Datuk Seri Mohammad Fakhruddin Mohd Arif.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Fakhruddin said Pekan Umno expressed its gratitude to Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim for granting the conditional pardon through the Pardons Board on Sept 18.
He said Pekan Umno would continue to pray for Najib's strength, good health and that his affairs would be eased.
"As a sign of our unwavering affection and support, Pekan Umno mobilised its leadership at every level to raise as much funds as possible beginning Sept 19.
"The total amount collected over 6 days since the fund was launched is RM36,204.15," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Traffic policeman hit by car while controlling traffic for Kelantan Sultan’s convoy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 22-year-old traffic policeman was injured after being struck by a car while controlling traffic for the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V’s convoy in Tumpat, Kelantan, yesterday.
The incident occurred at about 1.25pm at the Kampung Kepulau traffic-light junction in Palekbang, where the officer from the Tumpat district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division was closing the road from Morak towards Palekbang.
According to
Harian Metro
, Tumpat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said the road closure was to allow Sultan Muhammad V’s convoy to pass as the Kelantan Ruler travelled to Friday prayers and a public feast held in conjunction with his 57th birthday celebrations.
“A Proton Saga driven by a 55-year-old local woman from the direction of Morak is believed to have failed to notice the police officer before hitting him,” Mohd Khairi said in a statement.
“The 22-year-old officer fell and suffered minor injuries.
“He was taken to Tumpat Hospital for outpatient treatment, while the driver was unhurt.”
Mohd Khairi said the case was being investigated under Section 79(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police are also seeking dashcam footage or other recordings that could assist investigations.
“We advise all road users to comply with instructions from police officers carrying out traffic control duties and to pay full attention to road conditions, particularly during special operations and traffic-control exercises, to prevent unwanted incidents,” he said.

Title: Moro Islamic Liberation Front says Malaysia’s role ‘indispensable’ to Philippines’ Bangsamoro peace process
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — After decades of facilitating the Bangsamoro peace process, Malaysia remains an indispensable and trusted ‘honest broker’ whose involvement should continue until the process reaches its conclusion, according to the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
MILF Peace Implementing Panel chairman Mohagher Iqbal said Malaysia had earned a high level of trust from both the MILF and the Philippine government through its impartiality and record in facilitating negotiations since 2001.
“Malaysia’s facilitation is indispensable. Malaysia is an honest broker, and since 2001, it has shown the way, journeying with the two parties, tackling and overcoming obstacles along the way,” he told a press conference here on Friday.
Iqbal said Malaysia had helped facilitate key agreements between the Philippine government and the MILF, including the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro and the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB).
The CAB, signed in 2014, paved the way for the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law and the establishment of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority.
“So there is no reason why Malaysia should not continue as the facilitating country. It has delivered,” he said.
With its track record and the confidence placed in its impartiality, Malaysia remained an important factor in bringing the peace process to its eventual conclusion with an Exit Agreement, he said.
“I would dare to say that without Malaysia as an honest broker, I don’t think we would have reached this far.
“Malaysia has been with the peace process since 2001. And we hope that Malaysia will continue to facilitate these talks until the Exit Agreement,” he said.
The Philippine government and MILF are working towards an Exit Agreement to formally conclude the peace process once all commitments under the CAB have been fulfilled.
Earlier, Iqbal attended a special meeting of the Government of the Philippines (GPH) and MILF Peace Implementing Panels on the implementation of the CAB.
The Philippine government delegation was led by Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity Secretary Mel Senen Sarmiento, while Iqbal headed the MILF delegation.
Malaysia’s facilitator in the peace process, General (R) Tan Sri Zulkifli Zainal Abidin, was also present. — Bernama

Title: Ahead of Budget 2027, Anwar invites small entrepreneurs to identify those needing support
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is allowing small entrepreneurs in every village to propose aid recipients following the government’s plan to increase the specific allocation for the group in Budget 2027.
He said the suggestions were crucial to ensure the aid reaches small traders who genuinely need it and have the potential to expand their businesses.
“I want to give small traders in every village the opportunity to suggest if there are other friends who should be given a chance... because in our Budget next month, God willing, I want to increase the allocation for these entrepreneurs,” he said when officiating the Kedah Usahawan Bangkit scheme at the Federal Government Administration Complex in Anak Bukit here yesterday.
Anwar said many stalls run by small entrepreneurs also provided employment, thereby helping to generate income for the local community.
“When we give aid to these small entrepreneurs, even if it is small, they work hard and truly appreciate the assistance given,” he added.
He said the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) would determine the best method to assist needy small entrepreneurs after receiving the proposals.
About 1,500 entrepreneurs and petty traders in Kedah gathered at yesterday’s event to support the Madani Government’s efforts in strengthening the people’s economy.
Through the Usahawan Bangkit scheme, the government provides business equipment aid tailored to the entrepreneurs’ needs to increase their business capacity and productivity.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue to attract major foreign investments to boost the country’s economy, while ensuring the entry of foreign companies does not affect local enterprises, especially small entrepreneurs.
“Although I bring in foreign investments, I do not disrupt small entrepreneurs...I don’t go overseas for no reason,” he said.
He said investments by major companies, including in artificial intelligence (AI), computing and semiconductors, could stimulate the country’s economic growth and offer more job opportunities for the people.
Anwar also cited the development of medical technology in China, which is currently capable of treating the blind and restoring their sight.
Meanwhile, the Prime Minister stressed that the government was continuously working to alleviate the people’s burden, particularly regarding the rising cost of goods. — Bernama

Title: Form Two student dies after being found unconscious at Kuala Pilah school hostel, bullying alleged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 14-year-old Form Two student died last night after being found unconscious at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, amid allegations from his family that he had been bullied.
Kuala Pilah district police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin confirmed the incident and said further details would be released soon, the
New Straits Times
reported.
According to the report, the student was found unconscious at the hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
His body was subsequently transferred to the Forensic Medicine Department at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital in Seremban for a post-mortem examination.
Berita Harian
reported separately that a woman claiming to be the boy’s aunt had posted about his death on Threads last night, alleging that he had been assaulted while at the school hostel.
The woman said she learnt of her nephew’s death after receiving a call from her younger sister, who is the boy’s mother.
“Angah called me earlier, crying, saying her son had died after being beaten at the school hostel.
“Everyone is now on the way to Kuala Pilah Hospital,” she wrote, according to
Berita Harian
.
In a subsequent post, the woman said the boy’s body had initially been at Kuala Pilah Hospital before being transferred to Seremban for a post-mortem.
She also alleged that a Form Four student had been detained in connection with the case.
Police have not publicly confirmed the alleged detention.
In another post this morning, the woman said the post-mortem examination was scheduled for noon.

Title: Anwar approves RM2.8m to repair Islamic education institutions in Kedah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional allocation of RM2.8 million this year to repair basic infrastructure at 14 Islamic education institutions across Kedah.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the allocation was to ensure students could study in a more comfortable and safe environment.
“The Madani Government will continue to uphold the eminence of Islam by strengthening Islamic education institutions and fostering the study and understanding of hadith in society,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
In the same post, Anwar also announced a RM250,000 allocation to implement hadith-related programmes.
He said both allocations would be coordinated by the Kedah Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM).
“Hopefully, this effort will benefit the students and continue to cultivate a culture of knowledge in society,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: China trip boosts investment prospects and trade ties for both nations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described his recent working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou as yielding significant results, particularly in harnessing investment potential and trade cooperation that will generate widespread benefits and prosperity for both Malaysia and China.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, stated that both countries must leverage their diplomatic relations — currently at an all-time high — to continue exploring opportunities and pioneering new, highly promising collaborations.
He noted that Malaysia’s participation in the WorldSkills Competition and Summit, as well as the Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE), has showcased the nation’s capabilities on the international stage.
“I also conveyed Malaysia’s firm stance that in the pursuit of artificial intelligence (AI) development and technological advancement, the foundations of humanity and values must not be sidelined.
“Amidst global competition that breeds uncertainty, we must move forward through dialogue and cooperation to build a fairer and more equitable world,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Anwar also expressed his commitment to continue driving the Madani Diplomacy Tour for the sake of the people and our beloved homeland, Malaysia.
The Prime Minister undertook a three-day working visit to China on Tuesday at the invitation of Chinese Premier Li Qiang, with two main agendas: attending the WorldSkills Shanghai Competition and the GDTE in Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: Anwar firm on non‑interference, says Negeri Sembilan ruler’s position must be decided under Constitution
Article:
PENDANG, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim stressed that he would not interfere in matters concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, and that any dispute involving the royal institution should be resolved in accordance with the Constitution and the law.
He said under the constitutional monarchy system practised in the country, any action concerning a Ruler could not be taken arbitrarily but must be based on constitutional provisions.
“I said I am not interfering. What am I interfering in? The Undangs made a decision. There are parties supporting them and giving their views, and there is no problem with that. I do not want to interfere.
“But even with the Undang, which is valid, which is invalid? Decide and resolve that,” he said during his speech at the Sebarkan Salam dan Pendang Berselawat Bersama Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim programme here last night.
Anwar said issues involving the Ruler should not be taken lightly as Malaysia practises a constitutional monarchy that places the royal institution within the framework of the Constitution.
He said any action to remove or depose a Ruler could not be taken lightly, but was instead subject to the conditions and processes stipulated in the state Constitution.
“Discuss it amicably. I do not agree with overthrowing a Ruler so easily. Our system cannot work that way, which is why the Constitution is very clear,” he said.
According to Anwar, the Prime Minister and Cabinet also have limits to their powers set by the Constitution and cannot arbitrarily change matters relating to the institution of the Malay Rulers.
“The Prime Minister is the chief executive administering the country. What is his limit? He cannot amend the Constitution regarding Islam, the Malay language, the rights of all Malays and the Rulers,” he said.
He said the principle must be defended to ensure the constitutional monarchy system was not eroded by actions that did not follow constitutional channels.
“If we can bring down a Ruler so easily, the royal system will cease to exist in our country. But I understand the people, especially the Malays, and many Malaysians, including the Chinese and Indians, also do not want this system to be threatened,” he said.
Anwar said the issue should not be regarded merely as a political issue, but involved the country’s system that must be defended.
“If we, as Malays, are divided even over the Malay Rulers as a pillar of our system, how can we expect others to respect us? This is our problem, because hatred, anger and differences of opinion have caused us to lose our judgement and our senses,” he said.
At the event, the Prime Minister also announced an additional allocation of RM2.8 million to repair basic infrastructure at 14 Islamic educational institutions throughout Kedah. — Bernama

Title: Weak 3.3-magnitude earthquake strikes Sabah’s Kuamut, no tsunami threat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.3 in magnitude was detected in the Kuamut area of Kinabatangan, Sabah, at 5.32am today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake was centred at 5.1 degrees north and 116.8 degrees east, at a depth of 118km.
Its epicentre was about 34km south-west of Tongod, Sabah.
MetMalaysia said the earthquake posed no tsunami threat to Malaysia.
Sabah experiences relatively frequent low-magnitude earthquakes because of its proximity to active seismic zones in the region.
Most recorded tremors are minor and do not cause serious damage.

Title: Piranhas in Pahang? What we know about the mystery fish found at Klau Dam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Piranhas are not native to Malaysia.
But that distinction has come into focus after fish suspected to be piranhas were reportedly caught around Klau Dam in Raub, Pahang, prompting the Department of Fisheries (DOF) to investigate whether the non-native fish may have been introduced into Malaysian waters.
So far, however, the department says there is no concrete evidence that a piranha population has become established at the dam.
So what exactly are piranhas, how dangerous are they, and how did fish resembling a species associated with South America come to be reported in Pahang?
Here is what we know.
What are piranhas?
Piranhas are freshwater fish belonging to the family
Serrasalmidae
, a group that also includes closely related fish such as pacus.
They are native to Central and South America, with many species occurring in major South American river systems, including the Amazon basin.
Exactly how many species qualify as piranhas is not straightforward because their taxonomy has been revised over time and scientists continue to distinguish between closely related species.
Among the best known is the red-bellied piranha, scientifically known as
Pygocentrus nattereri
.
That is the species cited in reports surrounding the Klau sightings, although Malaysian authorities have yet to confirm the identity of the fish caught there.
Why are they known for their teeth?
Piranhas are recognisable for their powerful jaws and sharp, interlocking teeth.
Red-bellied piranhas have a particularly distinctive appearance, with a reddish underside and teeth adapted for cutting pieces from prey.
They eat fish and a variety of other animals, including shrimp, worms and molluscs.
Their diet varies between species, however, and piranhas are not simply specialised predators that spend their lives hunting larger animals.
Their reputation as ferocious man-eaters has also been exaggerated.
National Geographic Kids
notes that although red-bellied piranhas can swim and hunt in shoals numbering more than 100, researchers believe grouping also provides protection rather than serving purely as a means of attacking prey. Reports of red-bellied piranhas attacking humans are extremely rare, according to the publication.
A 2025 study published in the
Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
also found that media portrayals have contributed to the perception of piranhas as relentless killers.
Researchers examined 711 reported human cases in Brazil over a 10-year period and found that 82.27 per cent were classified as mild.
The study found that most reported injuries were mild and commonly involved single bites, while reports also associated incidents with factors including breeding behaviour and the improper disposal of food into rivers.
Do piranhas really eat people?
Piranhas can bite humans, but the popular image of shoals stripping people to the bone is largely a product of folklore and sensationalised portrayals.
That does not mean they are harmless.
Some species can inflict painful bites, particularly when defending nests or young, or when environmental conditions and human activity affect their behaviour.
The 2025 Brazilian study found that 29.62 per cent of the reported cases examined occurred during the breeding season, while 25.92 per cent were associated with the improper disposal of food in rivers.
In other words, the presence of piranhas does not automatically mean swimmers face an attack by a school of fish.
How big can they get?
The red-bellied piranha can grow to about 14 inches, or roughly 36cm, according to
National Geographic Kids
.
What else is unusual about them?
Red-bellied piranhas can communicate through sound.
When aggressive, some produce bark-like sounds as a warning to other piranhas to keep their distance.
Females can also lay thousands of eggs.
The Fisheries Department warns that alien fish species can disrupt local ecosystems and threaten native fish populations if released into public waters. — Picture via Department of Fisheries
So are piranhas found naturally in Malaysia?
No. Piranhas are not part of Malaysia’s natural freshwater fauna.
Their presence in Malaysian waters would therefore represent the introduction of a non-native species.
The DOF lists piranhas among alien fish that must not be released into public waters. Its fisheries database also names other non-native species including pacu, arapaima and peacock bass among fish that cannot be released.
The department has warned that alien species can affect native fish populations and disrupt aquatic ecosystems if they become established.
What happened at Klau Dam?
The current concerns began after a fish suspected to be a piranha was caught at Klau Dam on August 26.
The fish was caught by a local resident using a cast net, and footage of the catch was subsequently circulated through a WhatsApp group.
On September 17, the DOF said its Fisheries Research Institute in Glami Lemi, Negeri Sembilan, had examined photographs and video recordings and found that the fish’s observable morphological characteristics were consistent with the genus Pygocentrus, which includes piranhas.
However, the department could not definitively identify the species because the physical specimen was no longer available. The fish had reportedly died and been discarded before investigators could examine it.
Monitoring by the Pahang Fisheries Department up to September 15 had also found no additional confirmed catches or related safety incidents.
Then, on September 19, angling group Jejak Air Tawar claimed that a second red-bellied piranha had been caught in Sungai Klau beneath a bridge.
The group identified the fish as Pygocentrus nattereri, but acknowledged that the discovery did not establish that the species had begun breeding in the river.
The claimed second catch has not been independently confirmed by the DOF.
What does the Fisheries Department say now?
As of its latest update on September 22, the department could still not conclusively identify the fish, although preliminary analysis of video footage found that its morphology more closely resembled a piranha than a pacu.
Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said the department would collaborate with Aquaria KLCC on DNA or environmental DNA, or eDNA, analysis to help identify the fish.
The collaboration would draw on ‘live’ piranha specimens and existing DNA information held by Aquaria KLCC.
Adnan said confirmation was not possible without a physical specimen.
The department has instructed inland fishermen around Klau Dam to retain and surrender any fish resembling a piranha for examination, including checks of its morphology, scales and teeth.
Adnan said there had been reports of similar fish being found by fishermen, but the specimens had already been discarded.
For now, the department says there is no concrete evidence that a population of the species has become established at Klau Dam, and there have been no reports of unusual deaths among local fish or attacks involving anglers or members of the public.
Could piranhas survive in Malaysia?
According to Adnan, if the fish is eventually confirmed to be a piranha, it could potentially adapt and reproduce in Malaysia because of similarities between Malaysia’s equatorial climate and conditions in its native habitat.
That does not mean a population has become established at Klau Dam.
Determining whether the fish was an isolated release, part of a small group or evidence of a reproducing population will require further investigation — and, importantly, confirmed specimens.
That is why the department is asking fishermen and members of the public not to discard suspected piranhas.
What has Malaysia done about alien fish before?
The Klau case is not the first time authorities have raised concerns about non-native fish.
In March, the DOF and police seized prohibited fish including arapaima, sturgeon, peacock bass, pacu and Amazon redtail catfish during inspections of ornamental fish premises along Jalan Pudu in Kuala Lumpur.
The operation involved 42 enforcement officers and resulted in seizures estimated at RM35,674.
The department said the species were considered high-risk because of their invasive potential and possible impact on local biodiversity if released into public waters.
What should anglers do if they catch one?
The DOF has advised that suspected alien fish should not be released back into the water.
Instead, fishermen and anglers who catch fish resembling piranhas around Klau Dam have been asked to retain the specimen and hand it to the Pahang Fisheries Department for examination.

Title: Kuching Marathon cancellation a blow to 13,000 participants who made travel plans, says Sarawak sports minister
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — Sarawak Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah has expressed disappointment over the last-minute cancellation of Kuching Marathon 2026, which had attracted more than 13,000 registered participants.
He said the decision was particularly difficult for participants from outside Sarawak who had made advance arrangements, including booking flights and accommodation.
“If it is indeed cancelled, I myself feel sad because of the hopes of those who came and registered. We also know that there are more than 13,000 participants.
“Many of them came from outside Sarawak and had already booked accommodation such as hotels and homestays. Some travelled by plane, which involved costs to attend the marathon,” he said when commenting on the cancellation.
Earlier today, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) announced that the event, scheduled for Sunday (Sept 27), had been cancelled due to the prevailing haze affecting Kuching and surrounding areas.
Abdul Karim said he had been at the race pack collection venue shortly before the announcement and had not been informed about the cancellation at the time.
However, he said he understood that the organisers would have had valid reasons for making the decision, possibly following advice from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC).
“I believe the organisers must have had certain reasons for cancelling it, possibly on the advice of PDRM and SDMC,” he said.
Abdul Karim said his ministry had also provided financial assistance towards the organisation of the event, although its implementation remained subject to various considerations.
He said he understood if the cancellation prompted criticism from participants, particularly those who had already made travel and accommodation arrangements.
At the same time, some participants had praised the organisers for prioritising public health and safety despite the decision coming shortly before the event.
Meanwhile, KMA said registered participants could collect their finisher medals and finisher tees tomorrow (Sept 26) and Sunday at the Alfresco area of Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre.
Collection will be available from 9am to 9pm tomorrow and from 8am to 1pm on Sunday.
Participants must present their physical race bib at the designated category counter to collect their finisher medal and, where applicable, finisher tee.
One person may collect the items on behalf of up to five participants, provided the physical race bibs of each participant are presented.
Participants who have yet to collect their race packs must do so before collecting their finisher medal and finisher tee.
Race pack collection will remain open on Sunday from 10am to noon. — The Borneo Post

Title: EC: 43,309 new voters added in August — check the electoral roll by October 24
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for August 2026 (DPT BLN8/2026) is open for review for 30 days until Oct 24, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus.
He said DPT BLN8/2026, which was gazetted yesterday, contains the names of 43,309 citizens aged 18 and above during the period from Aug 1 to 31, 2026, who were automatically registered as new electors.
Khairul Shahril said it also includes 34,411registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies and 2,728 voters who have changed their voter category or status.
He urged voters in the relevant categories to check their names in the DPT BLN8/2026.
“Checks can be made via the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my or https://mysprsemak.spr.gov.my, the official state election office portal at http://ppn.spr.gov.my, the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, the MySPR Semak mobile application, or the Voter Registration Check hotline at 03-8892 7218,” he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril said those who find that their names are not listed in the DPT BLN8/2026 may submit a claim by completing Form C through the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my or by visiting the relevant State Election Office.
Any registered voter in an electoral constituency who, after checking the roll, wishes to object to the inclusion of the name of a voter who has transferred into the constituency may do so by completing Form D through the same channels.
Forms C and D can also be downloaded from the State Election Office portal at http://ppn.spr.gov.my and submitted to the relevant state election director, together with the objection fee, during office hours throughout the DPT BLN8/2026 review period. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s Asian Games sepak takraw gold after 36-year wait
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the national men’s sepak takraw squad on winning the team regu gold medal at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
He described their success in ending the country’s 36-year wait to reclaim the gold medal, which was also Malaysia’s fourth gold at Asiad 2026, as a highly meaningful victory and a source of pride for all Malaysians.
“
Syabas
(Well done) Malaysia. Continue to bring glory to Malaysia,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, the national sepak takraw squad clinched the men’s team regu gold medal after defeating Thailand 2-0 in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Arena.
Malaysia last won gold in the event when they defeated the same opponents at the 1990 edition in Beijing. — Bernama

Title: Immigration detains 84 foreign nationals in two-phase raid at Putrajaya’s ‘Green Flats’
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Immigration Department detained 84 foreign nationals under Ops Pintu at Pangsapuri Putra Harmoni, better known as the “Green Flats”, here following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs.
It said 60 Immigration personnel conducted the operation in two phases beginning yesterday.
“The first phase of the operation began at 11.30am yesterday, with business premises in the apartment area inspected and enforcement action taken.
“The operation resumed at 1.3 am today, with residents suspected of being illegal immigrants as the main target,” it said in a statement today.
It said 321 people were inspected, while 84 foreign nationals — 73 men, nine women and two children — were detained for further investigation.
“Intelligence gathering revealed the presence of foreign nationals residing in the area, with some believed to be conducting business activities there,” it said, adding that Ops Pintu was a continuation of enforcement operations in settlements identified as having a high density of foreign nationals, following an operation conducted on September 9.
As such, the department urged owners of houses and premises to be responsible for their tenants and ensure that the immigration status of occupants or tenants is valid and complies with the stipulated requirements.
“At the same time, the public is encouraged to continue providing information regarding the presence of illegal immigrants or activities suspected of violating the law,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Bar seeks disclosure of taxpayer cost of Najib house arrest, plans fresh court challenge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Malaysian government should disclose the additional cost to taxpayers if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak serves the remainder of his SRC International jail term under house arrest, Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj said today.
In a statement, Anand urged the Federal Territories Pardons Board and the Prime Minister’s Department to disclose two things to the public:
“Declassify and publish the official minutes of the Pardons Board meeting(s) held regarding Najib’s First Pardon and Najib’s Second Pardon decisions”; and
“Fully disclose all conditions proposed to be attached to Najib’s house arrest, including monitoring protocols, enforcement authorities and the additional costs to taxpayers that a ‘house arrest’ would entail.”
In calling for greater transparency, Anand said the Malaysian Bar had adopted a joint statement issued on September 22 by 37 civil society groups and 387 individuals, including former Bersih leaders Datuk Ambiga Sreenevasan and Maria Chin Abdullah, as well as Martabat PJ.
The joint statement urged the Pardons Board to release the full minutes and recorded justifications for its decision-making process in relation to Najib’s two pardons, under which his SRC sentence was first reduced and he was subsequently allowed to serve the remainder under house arrest if he fulfils certain conditions.
Anand also announced today that the Malaysian Bar would go to court to challenge the Pardons Board’s decision and advice concerning Najib’s second pardon.
“The Malaysian Bar will, through its solicitors, challenge the decision and advice of the Pardons Board concerning the Second Pardon, while maintaining its appeal in relation to the Pardons Board’s decision and advice on the First Pardon,” he said.
Najib has been imprisoned since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
The first pardon referred to by Anand was the January 2024 decision that reduced Najib’s 12-year jail term to six years and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
The second, granted on September 18, allows Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided he pays the RM50 million fine and complies with other conditions.
Najib remains in prison as he has yet to pay the RM50 million fine.
His lawyer, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said today that Najib could not afford to pay the fine, noting that his bank accounts remain frozen.
Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj has called for the full conditions and taxpayer costs of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest to be disclosed, as the Bar prepares a fresh legal challenge over the former prime minister’s second pardon. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
About ‘house arrest’ in Malaysia
Among other things, Anand noted that then High Court judge Alice Loke had ruled in a court case involving Najib that Malaysia has no legal mechanism for house arrest.
He said the home minister had also confirmed that there was no law providing for house arrest, while the Cabinet had approved in principle the drafting and tabling of legislation on house arrest.
Addressing claims involving the purported house arrest of Kenneth Lee Fook Mun, a grandson of Tun H.S. Lee, Anand said the case was not a “legal precedent for granting house arrest” or legal authority for the proposition that Malaysia has a formal house-arrest framework.
Anand said Lee’s case did not appear to have been tested or endorsed by a court, and that it remained unclear whether his purported house arrest arose from a Pardons Board decision or from a release on licence by the Commissioner General of Prisons under Section 43 of the Prison Act 1995.
“Finally, from our research to date, there appear to be no standard operating procedures or guidelines in place for ‘house arrests’. A whole new ecosystem of rules and procedures would be required to operationalise ‘house arrests’,” he said.
Status of Malaysian Bar’s existing court challenge to Najib’s first pardon
On April 26, 2024, the Malaysian Bar filed a court challenge against Najib’s first pardon, which reduced his SRC sentence.
In that case, the Malaysian Bar sought to challenge the validity of the Pardons Board’s 2024 decision and advice.
It also sought a court order prohibiting the Pardons Board from considering any further pardon for Najib “until all criminal proceedings against him have been exhausted, and until he has publicly accepted responsibility for his actions and expressed repentance and remorse”.
As the challenge was brought through judicial review, the Malaysian Bar first had to obtain the court’s leave to proceed with the case.
The High Court on November 11, 2024, refused leave for the Malaysian Bar to proceed with the challenge.
The Court of Appeal is scheduled to deliver its decision on January 7, 2027, on the Malaysian Bar’s appeal against the High Court ruling.

Title: EC denies report of 15 new parliamentary seats for Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) has denied a report claiming that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased, saying there is currently no proposal to alter the number of federal seats in the state.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said no documents had been shared indicating that Sarawak’s parliamentary constituencies would be increased to any particular number.
“The EC wishes to emphasise that there is currently no proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies involving areas in Sarawak, as alleged by the newspaper to involve discussions related to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63),” he said in a statement.
Khairul Shahril said the only redelineation exercise currently being undertaken by the EC was the Seventh Sarawak Electoral Constituency Redelineation Review, with its proposals being displayed for public inspection from September 1 to 30.
The review proposes 17 new state constituencies, increasing the number of Sarawak Legislative Assembly seats from 82 to 99, as well as changes to the names of several existing state constituencies and one parliamentary constituency.
He urged the public to refer only to verified information on the redelineation exercise through the EC’s official portal and statements issued by the commission.
The denial follows a Berita Harian report earlier today claiming Sarawak could see 15 new parliamentary constituencies under a proposed electoral redelineation exercise, which would increase the state’s representation in the Dewan Rakyat from 31 to 46 seats.
The report said the proposal was aimed at moving Sabah and Sarawak’s combined parliamentary representation towards one-third of the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the MA63. — The Borneo Post

Title: MACC completes Kedah fertiliser probe, two may face charges soon
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed its investigation into the delayed supply of fertilisers in Kedah, with two individuals set to be charged soon in connection with the case.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the charges will be brought under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009, which pertains to misappropriation and false documents.
“The MACC investigation into the issue of fertiliser distribution to farmers and paddy planters in Kedah has been completed.
“We will refer the case to the Attorney General, and if consent is granted regarding our recommendation, the charges will likely be registered in court next week or the week after,” he told a press conference after the closing ceremony of the 5th National Governance, Integrity, and Anti-Corruption Research Conference 2026 here today.
Abd Halim, however, did not reveal the identities of the individuals to be charged.
On September 7, the MACC opened an investigation paper into the delayed distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser, or Paddy Fertiliser 3, to Kedah paddy farmers. The investigation followed a complaint lodged by the Malaysian Paddy Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (PeSAWAH) on August 26.
The delay by the supplier appointed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) affected paddy farmers across a 100,000-hectare area under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA). — Bernama

Title: MACC chief: Two former Felda officials to be charged over Kuala Lumpur Vertical City project next week
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — Two individuals being investigated over alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project linked to Felda will be charged next week, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said.
He said the two were a former Felda general manager and a former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Committee, also known as Felda Investment Commission.
"The Attorney General has given consent to charge the two individuals involved. The former Felda general manager will face one charge under Section 420, and the charge will be registered in court on September 30.
"The other individual, the former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Committee or Commission, will face two charges under Section 417, and the charges will be brought on September 29," he told a press conference after the Fifth National Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference closing ceremony here today.
The KLVC investigation is among seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.
The investigations focus on asset purchases and investments by Felda and FIC between 2010 and 2020, which are suspected to involve elements of corruption, misappropriation and abuse of power. — Bernama

Title: More questioning awaits Isa Samad in Felda probe once he recovers from eye surgery, says MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will resume recording the statement of Datuk Seri Isa Samad once the former Felda chairman recovers from a medical procedure.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Isa is being treated at the Serdang Hospital after undergoing eye surgery.
“Regarding Isa’s statement, we had to put it on hold. It was supposed to be recorded yesterday and today, but since he is unwell, we have postponed it until we receive information on his health status from the Prisons Department.
“Once he has recovered, we will continue recording his statement. There is still a lot that needs to be recorded from him,” he told a press conference after the closing ceremony for the 5th National Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference here today.
Earlier, the media reported that the MACC confirmed it recorded Isa’s statement at the Sungai Buloh Prison on September 17 to assist in investigations into the Op Fella case.
Abdul Halim said the statement was recorded in connection with Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FICSB)’s purchase and investment of assets, which are suspected to involve elements of corruption and misappropriation. — Bernama

Title: Witness tails fleeing hatchback after attempted theft, helping police make arrest in Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — A witness who followed a hatchback believed to have been used by two men fleeing an attempted vehicle component theft helped police trace their movements and arrest one suspect here last night.
Padawan district police chief Supt Barry William said the incident occurred at about 8.40am yesterday at a workshop along Jalan Batu Kawa here.
He said the witness spotted two men allegedly attempting to steal components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop.
“A witness noticed two suspicious men trying to steal the components from a vehicle parked outside the workshop before they fled using the hatchback after being confronted.
“The witness, who is the driver of a four-wheel drive (4WD) managed to track down and tail the hatchback, thus helping police trace the suspects’ movements,” he said in a statement.
The hatchback was later found abandoned in Jalan Rantau Panjang.
Police subsequently arrested one of the suspects, a 25-year-old man, at about 9.15pm the same day.
A metal box and car key were also seized to assist investigations.
Police are continuing efforts to track down the other suspect or suspects believed to be involved.
The case is being investigated under Section 379 read with Section 511 of the Penal Code for attempted theft. — The Borneo Post

Title: MACC to issue asset declaration notices to Saravanan, his wife and three children
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will issue notices to former human resources minister Datuk Seri M Saravanan, his wife, and their three children to declare their assets within a month.
Its chief commissioner, Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, said that the asset declaration notice under Section 36 of the MACC Act 2009 will be delivered on Monday to Saravanan, his wife, and their two children, while another child who is still abroad will receive it in November.
“They have been informed and will attend the MACC headquarters for the delivery of the notices.
“A period of 30 days (for asset declaration) is given, and if that period is insufficient, an extension will be granted if they apply,” he said at a press conference after the closing ceremony of the 5th National Level Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption 2026, here today.
Saravanan was previously charged in the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court with three counts of receiving bribes amounting to nearly RM1.09 million related to the approval of 1,000 foreign worker quotas for a company, four years ago.
In another development, Abd Halim said his side has not yet received the asset declaration from the former chairman of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, and his family.
“We just submitted the notices on Sept 15. Wait for a month,” he said.
The MACC served asset declaration notices on Abdul Azeez and his family under Section 49 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorism Financing Act 2001. — Bernama

Title: Perak court fines buyer, petrol station owner RM25,000 each over RON95 sale to Singapore car
Article:
MANJUNG, Sept 25 — An oil palm plantation worker and a petrol station owner were each fined RM25,000 by the Sessions Court here today for their involvement in buying and selling RON95 petrol for foreign-registered vehicles.
Judge Azizah Ahmad handed down the sentence against Wong Ing Wan, 46, and Ling Mei Yen, 51, after they pleaded guilty to the charges and also sentenced them to two months in prison if they failed to pay the fine. Both paid the fine.
Wong was charged with violating Regulation 4(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for purchasing 27.452 litres of RON95 petrol for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle.
He was accused of committing the act at the Siew Service Station in Ayer Tawar at 8:25pm on May 13 under Regulation 4(3) of the same Regulations, punishable under Section 22(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961, which carries a fine not exceeding RM1 million, a maximum prison term of three years, or both for a first offence.
Meanwhile, Ling was charged — at the same date, time, and location — with violating Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) for selling the same petrol to Wong for use in a foreign-registered (Singapore) vehicle.
The charge was filed under Regulation 3(2) of the similar Regulations, punishable under Section 22(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961, which provides for the same penalty.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Nazreen Zabarudin requested the court to impose a proportionate sentence on the two unrepresented accused, taking into account public interest and the fact that the case involved the controlled substance RON95.
He added that the offence involving the sale and purchase of petrol using the BUDI Madani quota had also gone viral and drawn public condemnation.
Wong and Ling pleaded for a lenient sentence as it was their first offence. The man noted he supports his wife, a child, and an elderly mother, while the woman cares for her 80-year-old father and three children who are still studying. — Bernama

Title: When will Melaka vote? EC to decide key state election dates on October 7
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on October 7 to discuss matters related to the 16th Melaka state election.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the special meeting followed the dissolution of the Melaka State Assembly last Wednesday.
“The special meeting will be chaired by EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.
“Matters to be discussed include key dates for the 16th Melaka state election, including the writ of election, nomination day, polling day, the electoral roll to be used, and other preparations for the election,” he said in a statement today.
He said a press conference would be held immediately after the meeting.
Last Tuesday, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the State Assembly effective Wednesday, after obtaining the consent of Melaka Governor Tun Mohd Ali Rustam. — Bernama

Title: Haze forces Kuching Marathon 2026 cancellation at eleventh hour
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Kuching Marathon 2026 scheduled for Sunday (September 27) has been cancelled due to the prevailing haze situation affecting Kuching and surrounding areas.
In announcing the cancellation, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) said it had been continuously monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and other environmental indicators since the onset of the haze.
It said the decision was made after consultation with relevant authorities and medical advisers, with the health and safety of participants, crew members, volunteers, officials, medical teams, and the public taking precedence.
“To honour the commitment of our runners, all registered participants may collect their finisher medal and finisher tee starting tomorrow at Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre (Alfresco Area),” KMA said in a statement.
It added that detailed collection schedules and instructions would be announced on its official social media platforms.
The cancellation came shortly after State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah visited the Kuching Marathon registration and race pack collection at Plaza Merdeka.
Map shows the route for what would have been the 42km full marathon. — Picture from Facebook/Kuching Marathon via The Borneo Post
When met by reporters, Abdul Karim had said the decision on whether the marathon could proceed would depend on the prevailing haze situation and assessments by the relevant authorities.
Abdul Karim, who is also State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister, said the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) had established indicators based on API readings to determine whether outdoor events could be safely held.
“I’m not in the capacity to say yes or no for the race to be conducted, because we in Sarawak do have the SDMC to determine whether an outdoor event should be held or not,” he said.
He also said more than 13,000 participants had registered for this year’s Kuching Marathon.
The first Kuching Marathon was held on August 17, 2014, and has since grown into one of Borneo’s largest international mass-participation running events.
Participation grew rapidly, surpassing 10,000 runners by 2019, with subsequent editions attracting participants from more than 40 countries. — The Borneo Post

Title: Woman dies after Honda Jazz loses control, crashes into lorry in Kulai
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 32-year-old woman with a hearing disability died after the Honda Jazz she was driving crashed into the rear of a lorry at KM32 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Air Hitam here early today.
The woman, who worked as a general worker at a technology park in Kulai, suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, while the 66-year-old local lorry driver sustained minor injuries,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the crash at about 6.15am.
“Initial police investigations found that the accident is believed to have occurred when the Honda Jazz driven by the victim, travelling from Kulai Besar towards Johor Bahru, lost control.
“The woman’s car then crashed into the rear of a lorry driven by a 66-year-old local man who was stopped at a traffic light,” he said in a statement.
Tan said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged anyone with information about the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Fatin Mohd Radzi at 018-3649199.

Title: PM’s brother Idrus Ibrahim buried in Bukit Mertajam after Friday prayers
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 25 — The remains of Idrus Ibrahim, the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, were laid to rest at the Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Muslim Cemetery here today.
The funeral was attended by hundreds of family members, relatives, friends and political leaders from various parties.
Earlier, the remains were taken from the family home at 12.20 pm in a van to the temporary prayer hall at Cheruk Tok Kun Bawah Jamek Mosque on Jalan Kolam.
The prime minister, accompanied by family members and members of the public, walked about 200 metres from the late Idrus’ home to the prayer hall.
The funeral prayers, held after Friday prayers, were led by Penang Mufti Assoc Prof Datuk Dr Mohd Sukki Othman. The remains were then taken to the cemetery and buried at 2.10 pm.
Penang Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah paid their respects to the late Idrus at the family home at 11.15 am.
Also present to pay their last respects were Penang Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid; Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development Minister and Bukit Mertajam MP Steven Sim; and political leaders from various parties.
Idrus died in his sleep at his residence at 6.10 pm yesterday. He was 83.
The former teacher is survived by his wife, four children and 10 grandchildren. — Bernama

Title: Vulnerable groups to be focus of Selangor Budget 2027, says MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Supporting vulnerable groups will be among the Selangor government’s main priorities in Budget 2027, with the aim of ensuring the state’s economic progress benefits people across all segments of society.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor’s development should go beyond strong economic performance and attracting investment to also addressing the needs of groups requiring greater attention, according to a
Berita Harian
report published today.
“We want to ensure that this state is not only developed with a good economy, that we are not only able to attract high investment, and that we can remain the ‘heartbeat of Malaysian economy’ or serve as an example in developing the artificial intelligence (AI), micro-business, microchip or semiconductor sectors.
“Instead, we need to look at specific groups that require attention so that the state’s economic progress and development are enjoyed fairly by the people of this state,” he said.
Amirudin said existing support programmes, including cash handouts and assistance under Bantuan Kehidupan Sejahtera Selangor (Bingkas) and YANIS, would be part of efforts to help vulnerable groups, including those affected by the current energy supply crisis.
He said this when summarising the Selangor Budget 2027 engagement session with the Selangor Menteri Besar at Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC), Section 14 in Shah Alam, today.
Amirudin said the first area of focus in the budget would be finding ways to assist vulnerable groups through a comprehensive support programme ecosystem while strengthening existing aid networks.
However, he said the challenge was to ensure that the support and programmes provided addressed the problems faced by vulnerable groups more accurately and meaningfully.
“Within the framework of looking at vulnerable groups, the groups at the top, or senior citizens and young people, are among those who deserve attention.
“Selangor is facing the challenge of becoming an ageing state in the near future, while every year people’s lifespan is increasing, and the birth rate is relatively…” he said.

Title: Appeals court lets MAIWP strike out man’s bid to change religion from Islam to Sikhism
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 25 — The Court of Appeal today allowed appeals by the Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) and the government to strike out a man’s suit challenging his religious status.
The three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid ruled that Shehzad Malik Muhammad Sarwar Malik’s case was a renunciation case and the relief he is seeking could only be granted by the Syariah Court.
“The respondent (Shehzad Malik) here cannot come to the Civil Court as the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to grant the orders,” said Justice Mohd Firuz, who delivered the unanimous decision.
He further said the court took the view that the respondent was legally identified as a person professing the religion of Islam, and the fact that he might not believe in the Islamic faith and did not practise Islamic teaching was irrelevant.
Earlier, the panel dismissed a preliminary objection raised by Shehzad Malik’s counsel contending that the appeals brought by MAIWP and the government were not proper before the court and should be struck out.
Justice Mohd Firuz held that the appeals are competent.
Shedzad Malik filed the originating summons in December 2023, claiming that at the time of his birth in June 1996, his parents professed the religion of Islam, but his mother had raised him as a Sikh.
He said that after his mother died in 2007, he was raised by his uncle, who also professed and practised Sikhism.
He is seeking a court declaration that his religious status according to the National Registration Department’s record be “amended and corrected” to Sikh instead of Islam, and that his name be changed from Shehzad Malik bin Muhammad Sarwar Malik to Bilawal Singh Bhutter.
On Oct 24 last year, the High Court dismissed MAIWP and the government’s applications to strike out the originating summons, prompting them to appeal to the Court of Appeal.
During the proceedings, lawyers Ahmad Kamal Abu Bakar and Arik Zakri Abdul Kadir represented MAIWP while Senior Federal Counsel Husniyyah Hanapi appeared for the government. Lawyers Sachpreetraj Singh Sohanpal and Amanda Sonia Mathew represented Shedzad Malik. — Bernama

Title: In Johor, Indonesian teen charged with trafficking over 25kg of illicit drugs
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 25 — A 19-year-old Indonesian male teenager was charged at the Magistrates’ Court here today with two counts of trafficking illicit drugs, suspected to be heroin and methamphetamine, weighing over 25 kilogrammes (kg) last week.
The accused, Nanda Afrizal, who is employed as a construction worker, nodded to indicate he understood the charges after they were read out before Magistrate Norasidah A. Rahman.
For the first charge, he is alleged to have trafficked drugs suspected to be heroin, with an estimated gross weight of 17,842 grammes, in a room at a house in Taman Lian Seng at 3pm on September 13.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act.
For the second charge, Nanda is alleged to have trafficked drugs suspected to be methamphetamine, with an estimated gross weight of 8,109 grammes, at the same time and location.
The offense was also framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and is punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act.
Both sections carry either the death penalty or life imprisonment upon conviction.
This includes 12 to 15 strokes of the cane depending on sentencing discretion and if death penalty is imposed.
In a separate charge, Nanda was also accused of possessing drugs suspected to be methamphetamine, with an estimated gross weight of 5.25 grammes, in the living room of the same house at the aforementioned time and date.
The charge was brought under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for illegal possession of drugs and is punishable under Section 39A(1) of the same Act.
The accused faces a prison sentence of not less than two years and not more than five years, as well as whipping of not less than three strokes and not more than nine strokes upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nik Noratini Nik Azman prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
The court did not offer bail and fixed November 25 for mention and submission of the chemistry report.
In the same proceedings, the accused faced a separate charge under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for allegedly remaining in the country without reasonable cause after the expiry of his social visit pass on October 8.
The offence is punishable under Section 15(4) of the same Act, which provides for a fine of not more than RM10,000, imprisonment for up to five years, or both upon conviction.
The accused was sentenced to eight months’ imprisonment from the date of his arrest after he pleaded guilty to the charge.

Title: Anwar wraps China visit with RM36.8b in trade, investment pledges
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, is not just a routine diplomatic trip, but rather a new benchmark for the continuation of strategic relations that strengthen cooperation in various fields between the two countries.
Amidst the global geopolitical and economic uncertainties, the MADANI Diplomacy approach brought by Putrajaya has proven to be fruitful, thus strengthening Malaysia's role as Beijing's main strategic partner in the Southeast Asian region.
The working visit at the invitation of the Chinese government not only strengthens bilateral relations, but also opens up new opportunities for Malaysia to expand investments, export markets and cooperation in strategic and high-value economic areas.
Among the main returns of the visit was the potential investment worth RM28.6 billion from meetings with 26 Chinese companies, including five of the republic's giants, particularly in high-impact sectors such as semiconductors, mainstreaming artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, electric vehicles (EV), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology and advanced manufacturing.
The commitment of companies such as robotics giants AgiBot Innovation, ZTE Corporation, Alibaba Group, Geely Automobile Holdings and Huawei Technologies to increase investment is based on confidence in the stability and policies implemented by the MADANI Government.
Also achieved as a result of this visit was the potential export to China worth RM8.2 billion for a period of one to three years.
Summarising the overall outcome of the visit, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the relationship between Malaysia and China is now at a very strong level and is developing positively.
Describing the close relationship between Malaysia and China today as having gone beyond the usual diplomatic framework, the Prime Minister said this bilateral relationship is based on mutual trust, sincerity and confidence in order to bring prosperity and benefits to the people of both countries.
During the packed working visit, Anwar stressed the long-standing trust and mutual confidence forming the basis of the Malaysia-China bilateral relationship and cooperation that goes beyond traditional diplomatic ties.
The Malaysia-China relationship also translates into a broader agenda covering connectivity, protection of local enterprises, the digital economy, and talent and skills development.
While delivering a keynote address at the plenary session of WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, Anwar said Malaysia has elevated Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) as the core of the country's industrial policy and an instrument of economic transformation, particularly in ensuring talent development goes hand in hand with investment inflows.
"Malaysia and China are well positioned to do more together. Investments come to Malaysia for various reasons. But we all know that it grows especially when there are sufficient skills to support it,” he said.
While in Hangzhou, Malaysia's first-ever participation in the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) provided exposure to the exploration of new technologies and AI applications that deserve to be learned and drawn from China's rapid progress.
Malaysia also offers a stable, well-connected and business-friendly base for partners from China and globally to forge strategic partnerships.
Malaysia's participation in both important Chinese events and Anwar's presence to deliver the keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 and GDTE is a high recognition for Malaysia and the country's leadership.
The Prime Minister had the opportunity to voice his stance on the importance of ethical digital technology, fair and free digital trade and shared prosperity through strategic national cooperation.
Anwar also expressed recognition of China's rapid progress in the fields of digital technology and AI as well as its role in sharing technological advances with countries in the Global South.
The bilateral meeting and discussions between the two Malaysian and Chinese delegations at the West Lake State Guest House, Hangzhou, highlighted the level of personal chemistry between Anwar and China Premier Li Qiang.
The close relationship between the two leaders is not a secret. Repeated meetings since Anwar's tenure as the country's leader in November 2022 reflect a high-level of mutual trust that goes beyond formal diplomatic protocols.
This closeness allows complex issues such as supply chains, the implementation of infrastructure projects and regional and international geopolitical stability to be discussed in a frank and relaxed, yet effective manner.
Among the matters discussed during the bilateral meeting was the agreement between Malaysia and China on the proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, Kelantan, thus providing economic spillover and prosperity to rural areas in Kelantan.
Also given attention was the concerns of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Malaysia regarding foreign market domination that could affect local interests.
"This matter has been raised directly and we have received assurances from the relevant companies, including Alibaba and Li himself, that the best method will be sought so that business dealings do not affect the interests of MSMEs in Malaysia," said Anwar.
This working visit not only maintains China's status as Malaysia's largest trading partner, but also redefines the landscape of cooperation from traditional commodity trade to the digital economy, artificial intelligence and high skills.
China has been Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) for the period January to August this year.
The combination of pragmatic MADANI Diplomacy and the close relationship between Anwar and Li puts Malaysia in the best position to maximise economic benefits for the well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Spell out the offence: Aminudin challenges Negeri MB over royal dispute allegations
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on current Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to specify the alleged shortcomings of the previous administration that led to issues involving the state’s customary traditions and royal institution.
Aminuddin said the public had the right to know what actions were allegedly not taken during his tenure as Menteri Besar, including the specific provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959 that were allegedly breached and when the alleged violation occurred.
"What actions were said to have been overlooked? Which provisions of the UUTKNS 1959 were allegedly breached and when did the alleged breach occur?
"If there was an offence, state clearly what it was. If there was a violation of the law, identify the relevant provision. On an issue of this magnitude, the public deserves clear and verifiable facts,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Aminuddin said he was prepared to take responsibility for decisions made during his tenure as Menteri Besar by providing relevant documents, dates and legal provisions based on official records.
Yesterday, Ismail said the issue in the state did not stem from the current administration but was a problem inherited from the previous government.
Meanwhile, the Port Dickson Member of Parliament also questioned Ismail’s decision to sign a proclamation document related to the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, despite previously choosing not to sign the same document.
Aminuddin said the proclamation document dated April 19 was presented to him on April 20 while he was still Menteri Besar, for his signature under Article 10(2) of the UUTKNS 1959.
"I decided not to sign the document. If I, as Menteri Besar at the time, could make that decision due to doubts over the process, how could the signature of the next Menteri Besar appear on the same document?
"Datuk Ismail, with his legal background, would certainly understand the importance of the process. The issue involving Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir is about whether the process was properly followed or had flaws from the beginning,” he said.
Aminuddin said Article 10 of the UUTKNS 1959 not only covers matters relating to the powers concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, but also sets out procedures that must be fulfilled, including matters related to a full and complete inquiry. — Bernama
